(C-L3) The Settings stylesheet comment describes two columns. (C-L4) D-152's line is `- None:`, with its dash, as `check-docs.py` requires. (C-L6) TRACEABILITY cites D-147 to D-153. Tests: `server/src/http/auth.test.ts` (every refusal in the 40 parallel guesses is `pin_paused` with Retry-After 600; a lock longer than the pause answers the pause with the lock's 960 s, then `locked_out` 360 s; the server PC changes the PIN during a pause), `client/src/dm/DmView.test.tsx` ('1 second', `lockedOutText` at 7,200 and 7,201 s, `locked_out` without Retry-After, the address last), `client/src/dm/SettingsDialog.test.tsx` (the short pause message, the intro replaced), `e2e/tests/window.spec.ts` (the rail overflowing with its lower edge marked, Redo brought into view by focus and uncovered, the upper edge then marked; the dialog fitting with a pause refusal and Change PIN, Sign out and Close reachable; the PIN signing in after the change; the test's asset deleted), `scripts/check-docs-plan.test.mjs` (the now-items rule: an empty Now accepted only with every package done and a `- None:` line; a done Now item refused). The dialog check failed with the U-M1 fix reverted (checked). (U-L3) The rail's toolbar role without arrow-key navigation predates REL-03 and is G-044.
payload.why: Critical and high findings block merge and there were none; the owner chose to fix every medium and low finding but the toolbar's arrow keys, which belong to UIX-01's rail and are recorded as a gap.
payload.alternatives: A monospace element for the address (not taken: the catalogue holds plain strings, and ending the sentence with it answers the copying problem); a thin visible scrollbar on the rail (not taken: the fade marks the hidden edge without widening the rail); refusing a non-loopback server in the seed command (not taken: a LAN address of the server PC is legitimate, and the warning says what it costs); starting the hours wording at three hours (offered, not chosen).

payload.title: Painted fog in place of fog regions
payload.source: The owner, in chat on 2026-10-01, after testing TBL-03: «at this point this feature is working with rectangular sets that i want to move into a paintbrush tool. I want the dm to be able with a paintbrush mark the regions that want to hide from players (also i want an eraser to be able to reveal hidden regions as well). I don't mind the mask to be client side as now working.» TBL-03 built named rectangles and polygons on grid corners, each fogged or revealed (D-144, `04` §13, `03` §1).
payload.question: Does a brush and an eraser replace the fog regions, and in what form: what the mask is made of, how the brush is sized, what happens to the regions already stored, and whether painting in preparation is undoable?
options: A) One painted fog mask per scene replaces the regions: the brush fogs and the eraser reveals, in cells of a quarter square each way so a round brush reads as freehand; Fog all and Clear all; the brush's radius set on a slider from a quarter square to five; the stored regions dropped by the migration; one stroke one undoable command on the live scene, none in preparation, as every other preparation edit → effect on scope: the Region entity, its four commands, three events and the region list leave; a mask on Scene, two commands and the fog event to both rooms replace them; the player filtering rule is unchanged but for the shape it reads.
B) Keep the regions and add the brush and eraser as a second layer → effect on scope: both models, their commands and two DM interfaces kept, and a token's visibility read from both.
C) Named painted regions, each fogged or revealed as a whole → effect on scope: a region gains a painted outline instead of a shape; erasing must choose a region; overlaps need a rule.
payload.recommendation: A, with preset brush sizes (half, one and three squares) cycled by [ and ], and the stored fogged regions converted into the mask, because one mask is the simplest model that answers the request and converting keeps what the DM already drew.

payload.answer: A, with the brush radius on a slider from a quarter square to five in steps of a quarter, and the stored regions dropped rather than converted

payload.title: TBL-04: painted fog replaces fog regions, the region table dropped
payload.decision: Q-101, answered by the owner: the fog regions of TBL-03 (D-144) are replaced by one painted fog mask per scene. The DM paints fog with a round brush and reveals it with an eraser, the radius on a slider from a quarter square to five; Fog all and Clear all cover the map. The mask is kept in grid units, in cells of a quarter square each way, on the scene (`scene.fog`, never part of the Scene contract, like `token_numbers`). The Region entity, the commands region.add, region.rename, region.setHidden and region.delete, the events region.added, region.updated and region.removed, the region routes and the region list leave; fog.paint and fog.fill replace the commands, each one undoable step on the live scene, and fog.updated carries the whole mask to both rooms. The players' rule is unchanged but for what it reads: a token is seen when not hidden and its centre is under no fogged cell, a centre on a cell's edge counting as inside; the server filters snapshots, events, numbering and image files by it as before, and the fog stays a mask the player view draws. Destructive migration plan (`09` §2, `14` §8): migration 0006 adds `scene.fog` (default no fog) and drops the `region` table in the same step; the regions already drawn are not converted, by the owner's choice, and the runner's dated backup of the database before migrating keeps them recoverable by hand. Painting in preparation goes over REST without undo, as every other preparation edit. A new package, TBL-04 in `13` §10, builds it; TBL-03 stays done as the record of what was built before.
payload.why: The owner tested the fog regions and asked for a paintbrush and an eraser instead (Q-101); a single mask is the simplest model that answers it and keeps the hidden-information rule in one place. Dropping the regions rather than converting them is the owner's choice: the data drawn so far is test data, and converting polygons needs code a SQL migration cannot hold.
payload.alternatives: Keeping the regions beside a brush (rejected by the owner: two fog models); named painted regions toggled whole (rejected by the owner: erasing would have to pick a region, overlaps need a rule); vector strokes replayed in order (rejected: storage grows with every stroke and the server replays them all to judge a token); whole-square cells (rejected by the owner: blocky edges); converting the fogged regions into the mask at start-up (recommended, not chosen by the owner); preset brush sizes (recommended, the owner chose a slider).

payload.title: TBL-04: how the painted fog is stored, painted, filtered, projected and drawn
payload.decision: Supersedes D-144, and the fog parts of D-145 (the revealed region's dotted outline, asking before deleting a region, drawing by keys), as D-154 decided. Mask (shared/src/fog.ts): cells of a quarter square each way in grid units, kept as rows of fogged [start, end) runs, sorted, apart and merged, no empty row, so equal fog is equal JSON; at most 2000 squares each way. A stroke is a mode (paint or erase), a radius from 0.25 to 5 in quarter steps and 1 to 1000 points in decimal grid units; it covers each cell whose centre lies within the radius of its polyline, worked out per row in closed form (a capsule's slice is one interval) and clipped to the map: a map's whole image by the grid's size and offsets (the size read from the columns before calibration), a map-less scene's columns and rows. Fog all fills that extent, Clear all takes every cell off. The client previews a stroke with the same function. Players' rule (seenByPlayers): not hidden and the token's centre under no fogged cell, a centre on a cell's edge judged by every cell it touches, so the rule errs toward hiding. Storage: migration 0006 adds scene.fog (JSON array, default '[]') and drops region; scene.fog is internal like token_numbers, outside the Scene contract, read by snapshots and GET /api/scenes/:id/fog; duplication copies it. Writes (server/src/db/fog.ts writeFog): a stroke, a fill or a restore in one transaction, with the token sight before and after and the numbering pass of D-144 unchanged; a write that leaves the mask equal is answered unchanged, sends nothing and records no undo step. Commands fog.paint {scene_id, stroke} and fog.fill {scene_id, fogged}, refused as scene_not_live off the live scene; undo and redo put the whole mask back (fog.restore, server-only). Events: fog.updated with the whole mask to both rooms, then token.removed for each token covered and token.added for each shown in ascending rank, as D-144 ordered them. REST in preparation: POST /api/scenes/:id/fog with {stroke} or {fill}, answering the mask; 409 scene_live on the live scene. Drawing: on the TV the mask is one path of rectangles (runs carried down the rows that repeat them) in #0A0806 with an 18 px soft shadow, its layer blurred 4 px by CSS so the cells' steps read as a round brush; in the DM view a dark tint under a blue hatch. The brush (F, or the rail's Fog brush): a drag paints or erases, a point every quarter radius, sent on release (a stroke past 1000 points is sent and continued); a right or middle drag pans; Enter paints at the view's centre, E switches, [ and ] step the radius, Escape drops the stroke under way, then leaves. A stroke sent stays drawn until the fog it made arrives, or is taken off when refused. The brush bar above the canvas holds Paint and Erase, a labelled range slider, Fog all and Clear all (each asked first; in preparation the dialog says there is no undo) and Done. The right panel's FOG group says how many tokens under the fog players cannot see, with Paint fog; a token's status says it is in the fog.
payload.why: D-154 and Q-101 as answered by the owner. Run-length rows keep a typical painted map to a few KB, a filled map to one run a row, and a point test to a binary search; a capsule per segment is the exact shape of a round brush moved along a line; one rule in shared code is still what the server filters by and the DM view counts by, so the hidden-information gate stays meaningful.
payload.alternatives: A bitmap per scene (rejected: its size follows the map, not the fog, and a 2000-square map would be megabytes); storing strokes and replaying them (rejected in D-154); sending only the cells a stroke changed (rejected: a whole mask keeps every view exact without ordering rules, and stays small); a canvas raster drawn at one pixel per cell and scaled (rejected: a large map's canvas would be too big); erasing with the same stroke leaving no slivers (not possible when the points differ; the DM erases with a wider brush).

payload.title: The token popover while the DM drags a token
payload.source: The owner, in chat on 2026-10-01: «selecting a token opens the details popover. If the DM then grabs the token to move it, the popover stays open, blocks the map and gets in the way of free movement.» and «Distinguish a click from a drag with a small movement threshold (about 4 px) … After the drop, the token stays selected but the popover stays closed. Clicking the token again reopens it … Also close the popover on Escape, on a click on empty map, and when panning starts (Space + drag).» `08` §11 shows a popover on the selected token whenever one is selected (UIX-01, D-140).
payload.question: When is the selected token's popover open: whenever a token is selected, or only after a click on it, closing on a drag of the token or a pan?
options: A) Opened by a click on the token (a press released within about 4 px), by choosing its row in the list, or by placing or duplicating it; a press that moves past the threshold is a drag, which closes the popover at once and leaves it closed after the drop with the token still selected; Escape, a click on empty map and the start of a pan close it too → effect on ux: the popover no longer follows the selection; a click on the selected token reopens it.
B) Keep it open while the token is selected, moved out of the way during a drag and back after → effect on ux: the popover still covers the map at the drop.
payload.recommendation: A, because it is what the owner described and it keeps the map free while a token moves.

payload.title: The token popover opens on a click and closes on a drag or a pan (Q-102)
payload.decision: Q-102, answered A by the owner: the selected token's popover is open only after a click on the token, a choice of its row in the list, or its placement or duplication; it no longer follows the selection. A press on a token that the pointer leaves by 4 px or more on either axis (the larger of the two distances, as Konva's `dragDistance` measures it) is a drag: no drag starts below it, and the drag's start closes the popover, which stays closed after the drop while the token stays selected; a release within it is a click and opens the popover. Pressing another token closes the open popover before selecting it, so a popover never carries over to the token pressed. A pan, whether by Space and a drag or by dragging the empty map, closes it at its start, and it stays closed when the pan ends; Escape and a click on empty map still let the token go and the popover with it. `08` §11's popover bullet is amended to say so. The threshold is `DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX` and `movedPast` in `client/src/canvas/tokens.ts`; the open state is the scene panel's, beside the selection.
payload.why: The owner reported that the popover blocks the map while a token is dragged and specified the behaviour; 4 px is the owner's figure and the usual click slop for a mouse or a pen, small enough that a deliberate drag is never read as a click.
payload.alternatives: Hiding the popover during the drag and showing it again at the drop (rejected: the owner wants it closed after the drop); a time threshold instead of a distance (rejected: a slow click is still a click); judging the distance by Euclidean length (rejected: Konva starts a drag by the larger axis distance, and the two rules must agree so that a press never both drags and opens).

payload.title: Eighteen condition markers with their rule text
payload.source: The owner, in chat on 2026-10-01: «Replace the current fixed set of 4 chips with a pinned set plus a searchable dropdown»: pinned Bloodied, Unconscious, Dead, Concentrating, Prone, Poisoned; in a «More…» list Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion (levels 1–6), Frightened, Grappled, Incapacitated, Invisible, Paralyzed, Petrified, Restrained, Stunned; markers as objects (`{ id, level }`), migrated; the list in a JSON data file with SRD rule text shown on hover; a distinct icon each from game-icons.net (CC BY 3.0) with an attribution line; at most 3 badges then «+N»; Dead greyed out, Invisible semi-transparent but still seen by players; no implied conditions applied. Asked whether this overrides the register, the owner chose «Approve as written», and an About & credits dialog in the DM view. `12` and `01` §9 allow four markers (Q-099), `01` §4 keeps every other condition Phase 2, and `01` §8 lets SRD 5.1 content in from Phase 2 only.
payload.question: Do tokens carry the eighteen markers the owner listed, with their SRD 5.1 rule text and bundled icons, before the release?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: eighteen markers, six pinned and twelve behind a searchable More… list, stored as objects with Exhaustion's level 1–6, the four stored markers migrated; the conditions' SRD 5.1 text (CC BY 4.0) and game-icons.net icons (CC BY 3.0) bundled, credited in an About & credits dialog; no implied condition applied; custom markers and durations left out → effect on scope: the marker set, its storage and contract widen; SRD content enters before Phase 2, for these rule texts only; still no rules in code.
B) Keep the four markers until Phase 2 → effect on scope: no change; the request becomes a Phase 2 item.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner asked for it in detail and approved overriding the register.

payload.title: TBL-05: eighteen condition markers stored as objects, with SRD 5.1 rule text and bundled icons
payload.decision: Q-103, answered A by the owner: a token's markers are eighteen conditions. Pinned in the popover, in this order: Bloodied, Unconscious, Dead, Concentrating, Prone, Poisoned. Behind a More… button, a searchable alphabetical list: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Incapacitated, Invisible, Paralyzed, Petrified, Restrained, Stunned. Active ones from the list show as selected chips too. `markers` becomes an array of objects, `{ id }`, or `{ id: 'exhaustion', level }` with level 1 to 6, each id at most once, kept in the order applied. `id` leaves room for a later `custom:<uuid>`, which is not built. The list is a data file, `shared/src/conditions.json` (id, label, pinned, icon, whether the text is the SRD's, rule text, implied conditions). It carries the SRD 5.1 text of the fifteen SRD conditions (CC BY 4.0) and a short original line for Bloodied, Dead and Concentrating. Implied conditions are named in the hover text and never applied. Icons are game-icons.net SVG paths (CC BY 3.0), bundled, credited with the SRD in an About & credits dialog in the DM view and in CREDITS.md. Drawing on both views: at most three badges, then +N, by priority Dead, Unconscious, Bloodied, then the rest in the order applied. Dead greys the token and strikes its label through. Bloodied keeps its ring and pulse. Concentrating keeps its dotted ring. Invisible draws the token semi-transparent on both views, players included, and is not the hide toggle. A hidden token's markers still never reach players. Data migration plan (`09` §2, `14` §8): migration 0007 rewrites every stored `token.markers` array of names into the same names as objects, in the same order. Lossless: the four old names are all among the eighteen. Rollback is the reverse map of each object's id; no data is dropped. The commands are unchanged: `token.setMarkers` carries the whole array and undo restores the previous one.
payload.why: The owner asked for this set and approved overriding the register entry that allowed four (Q-099) and the Phase 2 placement of other conditions and SRD content (`01` §4, §8). Objects carry Exhaustion's level and leave room for custom markers without another shape change. The rule text is read, never applied, so the MVP still has no game rules in code.
payload.alternatives: Keeping string ids with a separate exhaustion field (rejected: the owner gave the object shape, and a second field multiplies the contract); hardcoding the list in components (rejected by the owner); drawing the icons by hand (rejected: the owner named game-icons.net, and hand-drawn icons at 14 px would be weaker); applying implied conditions (rejected by the owner).

payload.title: TBL-05: how the eighteen markers are listed, validated, drawn and credited
payload.decision: Implements D-157. List: `shared/src/conditions.json` holds, per condition, id, label, pinned, icon (game-icons.net source, author and the SVG path on a 512-unit square), srd, rule (one line per paragraph or bullet) and implies; `levels: 6` on Exhaustion. The SRD text of the fifteen SRD conditions was taken from the 2014 SRD 5.1 conditions in the 5e-bits/5e-database data set (MIT), not retyped. Labels and rule text are data, not catalogue strings, as the owner asked; the sentences around them ("Also means: … (not applied).", "{label} (level {level})") are the catalogue's. Icons: Bloodied lorc/drop, Unconscious delapouite/night-sleep, Dead sbed/death-skull, Concentrating lorc/concentration-orb, Prone sbed/falling, Poisoned lorc/poison-bottle, Blinded delapouite/blindfold, Charmed lorc/charm, Deafened skoll/hearing-disabled, Exhaustion lorc/oppression, Frightened lorc/screaming, Grappled lorc/grab, Incapacitated skoll/breaking-chain, Invisible delapouite/invisible, Paralyzed sbed/electric, Petrified lorc/stone-block, Restrained lorc/fishing-net, Stunned delapouite/knocked-out-stars; each checked legible at 14 px. Contract (`shared/src/conditions.ts`): MarkerSchema is `{ id }` of a non-Exhaustion id, or `{ id: 'exhaustion', level }` with an integer level 1–6, strict; MarkersSchema an array of at most 18, unique items; `normaliseMarkers` keeps each id's first marker, in the order sent, and drops anything else, so the server stores each condition once in the order applied; `sameMarkers` compares order and level, so the same set again tells nobody. Popover: six pinned chips, then a pressed chip for each other condition carried, then More…, a search combobox over the twelve others in alphabetical order (arrows, Enter, Escape; keys typed there never reach the map); Exhaustion turned on starts at 1 and its chip gains a − level + stepper, − at 1 turning it off; each chip's and option's title is its rule text with the implied conditions named. Canvas: badges 14 px across on the DM's screen, in a row along the token's top edge a pixel apart, so none overlaps another or the label however small the token is drawn; Dead, Unconscious, Bloodied first, then the order applied, three at most and a +N badge last; Exhaustion's badge carries its level on a small disc; the hidden badge moves to the token's right edge, clear of the row; Invisible draws the token's body at 45% opacity on both views; Bloodied's ring and pulse and Concentrating's dotted ring stay. About & credits: an info button in the header opens a dialog with the AGPL notice, the icons' authors read from the list and the SRD 5.1 attribution, with no link outside the LAN; CREDITS.md says the same.
payload.why: One data file is the single source the owner asked for, and both server and client read it from `shared`. Normalising rather than refusing a duplicate keeps the old fixed-order tolerance of TBL-02. A row of badges, unlike the earlier arc on the token's left, stays readable on the TV, where a 30-square map draws a token about 36 px wide and three badges would otherwise overlap one another and the label.
payload.alternatives: An arc or a column of badges on the left (rejected: they overlapped on small tokens in the screenshots); condition labels in the message catalogue (rejected: the owner asked for them in the data file); a native select for More… (rejected: no search, and no icons in its options); refusing a duplicate id with validation_failed (kept for exact duplicates through uniqueItems; a same id with another level is normalised).

payload.title: TBL-05 review fixes: a condition named twice refused, migration 0007 safe to run again, the removed Exhaustion named at its level
payload.decision: Refines D-158, which stays in force except as stated. Review of TBL-05 (prompt 2, security and isolation, 2026-10-01): no critical or high finding, one medium, three low. (M1) Two Exhaustion markers at different levels passed the schema, whose uniqueItems compares whole objects, and one was silently dropped; the REST PATCH and `token.setMarkers` now refuse any set that names a condition twice with validation_failed (`repeatsCondition` in shared), so D-158's 'a same id with another level is normalised' no longer holds; tests in `server/src/ws/markers.test.ts`, `server/src/http/tokens.test.ts` and `shared/src/conditions.test.ts`. (L2) Migration 0007 rewrites only arrays that still hold names, so running it again over converted rows changes nothing; `server/src/db/schema.test.ts` runs it twice. (L3) Removing Exhaustion announces the level it had, not level 1. (L4) No-op detection confirmed sound; no change. Also confirmed with no finding: the players' projection unchanged and strict, every REST and live path validated, nothing outside the LAN, no markup from the data, and no trademark in UI text (`CREDITS.md`'s SRD attribution URL is the licence's own wording, in a repository document).
payload.why: A body the server answers ok but stores differently breaks the contract that each condition appears once; a migration that empties data on a second run is a hazard on restore.
payload.alternatives: Restructuring MarkersSchema to make ids unique in JSON Schema (rejected: no portable keyword compares one property across items); normalising the duplicate silently (rejected by the review).

payload.title: An initiative tracker before the release
payload.source: The owner, in chat on 2026-10-01: «Initiative tracker (DM side + TV strip) … Do not add any dice rolling. The table rolls physical dice, and the app only records the order.»; one entry per player character plus «one DM entry» labelled «Enemies» whose members (visible monster and npc tokens not marked Dead) are «computed live, never stored»; eight server commands `encounter.start`, `.end`, `.reorder`, `.setInitiative`, `.next`, `.previous`, `.addEntry`, `.removeEntry`, «each one … undoable, synced, and included in the snapshot on reconnect»; an Initiative panel in the DM view and «a slim strip along the top edge» of the TV that must «never reveal how many enemies there are or which ones»; «Not in this task: Dice, HP tracking, condition durations, per-monster initiative.» Asked whether this overrides the register, the owner chose «Approve as written». `01` §4 lists an initiative tracker in Phase 2, which MUST NOT be implemented in the MVP, and `11` marks it Future.
payload.question: Is the initiative tracker the owner described built before the release, overriding its Phase 2 placement?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: one encounter per scene with one entry per player character and one Enemies entry for the DM, ordered by the initiative numbers the table rolled or by dragging, turns and rounds advanced by the DM, eight undoable live commands, an Initiative panel in the DM view and a strip along the top of the TV that names no enemy; no dice, hit points, condition durations or per-monster entries → effect on scope: the live command set, the snapshots and both views widen; initiative leaves Phase 2; still no rules in code and no dice.
B) Keep the initiative tracker in Phase 2 → effect on scope: no change; the request becomes a Phase 2 item.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner asked for it in detail and approved overriding the register.

payload.title: Where an encounter is kept
payload.source: The owner's request of 2026-10-01 for Q-104 gives «One `Encounter` per scene» with `scene_id`, `active`, `round`, `current_index` and `entries`, and asks that End combat be confirmed «because it can't be undone across sessions». `03` §1 and `12` fix the entities stored in SQLite; the camera, ruler and undo history live in memory only (`04` §8, §9, §11).
payload.question: Is a scene's encounter stored in SQLite, or kept in the server's memory like the camera and the ruler?
options: A) In SQLite, one row per scene in a new `encounter` table added by an additive migration, deleted with its scene → effect on data: a ninth entity; combat survives a server restart and a switch to another scene and back.
B) In memory only, one per scene → effect on data: no new entity or migration; combat survives a scene switch but not a restart.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner's request gives the encounter a scene and a lifetime beyond the live session, and the migration is additive.

payload.title: An empty Enemies entry on Next
payload.source: The owner's request of 2026-10-01 for Q-104 says both «The DM entry is skipped automatically when it has no members» and «When no enemies are left at the start of the DM turn, show a prompt: "No enemies left. End combat?" with End combat / Continue»; an empty DM turn that is always skipped never starts, so the prompt could never show.
payload.question: When Next reaches the Enemies entry and it has no members, is it skipped, or does the DM's turn start with the prompt?
options: A) It stops there with the prompt when this encounter has had at least one enemy, Continue moving on to the next entry; while no enemy has yet been seen (an ambush still hidden) it is skipped silently → effect on ux: the prompt shows once the enemies are all dead or gone; an encounter started before the monsters are revealed runs through the players' turns alone.
B) Always skipped, and the prompt shown whenever it was skipped → effect on ux: the prompt also shows before any enemy is revealed.
C) Always a stop with the prompt → effect on ux: the DM answers the prompt every round until an enemy appears.
payload.recommendation: A, because it keeps both of the owner's sentences: the prompt when the enemies are gone, the skip while none has appeared.

payload.title: TBL-06: an initiative tracker, one encounter per scene stored in SQLite, with a DM panel and a TV strip
payload.decision: Q-104, Q-105 and Q-106, each answered A by the owner. A scene holds at most one encounter, a row of a new `encounter` table (`03` §1): `scene_id` (unique, deleted with the scene), `active`, `round` from 1, `current_index`, `enemies_seen` and `entries`, a JSON array in turn order. An entry is `{ id, kind: 'pc', token_id, initiative }` or the one `{ id, kind: 'dm', initiative }`, the initiative an integer or null; `kind` leaves room for a later `monster` entry, which is not built. The Enemies entry's members are computed from the scene's tokens whenever needed: monster and npc tokens players can see (`04` §4) that do not carry Dead. Eight live commands, each undoable and naming the live scene (`04` §2, §14): `encounter.start`, `encounter.end`, `encounter.reorder`, `encounter.setInitiative`, `encounter.next`, `encounter.previous`, `encounter.addEntry`, `encounter.removeEntry`; one event, `encounter.updated`, carrying the whole row to the DM and, to players, only a projection: the round, the entries of player characters they can see and the Enemies entry, which has the turn and which is next; no initiative number, member, count or `enemies_seen`, so a player view learns nothing it could not see on the map (`04` §4). Both snapshots carry the encounter. Deleting a token removes its entry in the same transaction, and undoing the delete puts the entry back. No dice anywhere. Data migration plan (`09` §2, `14` §8): migration 0008 creates the `encounter` table and its index; additive, nothing existing is read or rewritten. Rollback is dropping the table, losing only encounters.
payload.why: The owner asked for the tracker in detail and approved overriding its Phase 2 placement (`01` §4). Stored per scene, combat survives a restart and a switch to another scene and back, as the owner's model of one encounter per scene implies; a table of its own keeps the scene row unchanged. Computing the members rather than storing them is what the owner asked, and keeps the enemies' list right whatever command reveals, hides, fogs or kills a token. A projection built on the server keeps the hidden-information rule: every field players receive follows from what they already see.
payload.alternatives: Keeping the encounter in memory like the camera and the ruler (rejected by the owner, Q-105); a JSON column on `scene` (rejected: it would widen every scene read and the duplication path); one entry per monster (rejected by the owner, left for later through `kind`); always skipping an empty Enemies entry, or always stopping on it (rejected by the owner, Q-106); sending players the members and filtering them in the client (rejected: filtering happens on the server, `04` §4).

payload.title: TBL-06: how the encounter is stored, decided, projected for players and shown
payload.decision: Implements D-160. Rules: `shared/src/encounter.ts` holds the contract (EncounterSchema, PlayerEncounterSchema, initiative an integer from -99 to 999 or null, at most 200 entries) and every rule, pure: `membersOf` (monster and npc tokens `seenByPlayers`, without Dead), `takesTurn` (a player character's entry while players see its token, whatever its markers; the Enemies entry while it has members or once `enemies_seen`), `stepTurn` (+1 past the last entry counts a round, -1 before the first takes one back and does nothing on round 1), `sortByInitiative` (stable: highest first, unnumbered below in their order, so a dragged tie stays), `followTurn` (the turn stays with its entry through any reorder), `startTokens` (player characters players see, in stacking order, the DM's list order), `changeOf` (what each command does, or why it is refused: `bad_request` for starting a running encounter, any other command with none running, adding a token that is not a visible player character or already entered, removing the Enemies entry; `order_mismatch` for a reorder that does not name every entry once; `not_found` for an unknown entry or token) and `playerEncounter` (the players' projection). The server applies `changeOf` inside one transaction with the scene's tokens and fog read in it (`server/src/db/encounters.ts`); the client's test server applies the same function. Storage: migration 0008, one `encounter` row per scene (unique index on `scene_id`, ON DELETE CASCADE), `entries` a JSON array checked by the contract on read; End combat keeps the row with `active` 0, no entries, round 1. Deleting a token drops its entry in `deleteToken`'s transaction, in preparation and live alike; the live `token.delete` answers `token.removed` then `encounter.changed`, and its inverse carries the encounter before, which the undo restores with the token. Every encounter command's inverse is `encounter.restore`, the whole encounter before (none for a start on a scene that had none), not on the wire. `enemies_seen` is set by the command itself and, after any other live command that changed something, by `noteEnemies`, which tells the DM room and is no step of the history. Events: the DM room hears `encounter.updated` with the stored encounter from the projection of each `encounter.changed`; players hear `encounter.updated` with `playerEncounter` only when it differs from what it was before the command (`tellEncounter` in `server/src/ws/live.ts`, after the command's own events), so a token's reveal, fog or Dead that changes who is next reaches them and a hidden token's change does not; REST changes reach them in the snapshot diff of `refresh`. Both snapshots carry it. DM view: a third right-panel tab, Initiative, named with the round while combat runs (`Initiative · R3`); rows with a grip, the token's thumbnail, the name, Now and Next tags, the conditions as icons, a number field committed on Enter or blur (empty clears it, anything else not a whole number in bounds goes back), Move up and Move down, and Remove; native drag and drop as the scene list; the Enemies row opening on its turn to its members, each selecting and centring its token; the prompt on the Enemies turn with no members, whose End combat ends at once, since the prompt is the question, and whose Continue sends Next; an offer per visible player character without an entry, dismissed per browser; End combat from the header asked in a dialog. Enter and Shift+Enter pass the turn from anywhere in the DM view but a field, a button, a link, a tab, a menu item or an open dialog. The map rings the turn's player character with a wide ember ring and glow and each member on the Enemies turn with a thin faint ring, drawn whatever tool is on; the DM's camera centres on the player character whose turn comes up. TV: `InitiativeStrip`, fixed at the top centre, about 9% of the screen's height at 1080 lines, clamp-sized by the viewport's height; a portrait from the token's display image (what players may already fetch), the name, the Enemies card with a crossed-blades icon, NOW and NEXT tags, the round at the left; it fades in on its own, 400 ms like the scene fade, and out over 400 ms when combat ends; none with reduced motion. The client's checks of an arriving encounter are written out, as `isFogMask` is, so TypeBox's format checks do not bring the URL they name into the bundle (`check-external-urls`).
payload.why: One pure rule set used by the server and the client's test server keeps the DM view's tests honest against the server's behaviour. Comparing the players' projection around every command, rather than deriving it from the encounter's own events, is what makes the strip follow a reveal or a death without an encounter command, and send nothing when only a hidden token changed: the hidden-information gate's recordings stay identical with and without hidden tokens. The prompt's own End combat does not ask again: the prompt is the confirmation the owner described.
payload.alternatives: Deriving members on the client from players' tokens (rejected: players must not learn which tokens are enemies, `04` §4); a players' event per encounter command (rejected: a hidden token's change would then be countable by the version counter); storing `current_entry_id` instead of `current_index` (rejected: the owner gave `current_index`; the turn follows its entry by id when the order changes); a confirmation after the prompt's End combat (rejected: a second question for the same answer).

payload.title: TBL-06: review fixes (the turn passed on removal, no Next named for an unseen turn, focus and strip markup)
payload.decision: Refines D-161 after the security and isolation review (prompt 2), which found no critical or high issue. Medium, fixed: removing or deleting the entry whose turn it is passes the turn as Next would, to the next entry that takes it and counting a round past the last, never to an Enemies entry that never had a member or a player character players cannot see (`withoutEntry` takes the turn view). Medium, fixed: while the turn is a player character players cannot see, the players' projection names no Next either, so numbering, moving or removing that unseen entry changes nothing they receive; tested in `server/src/ws/encounter.test.ts` and `shared/src/encounter.test.ts`. Low, fixed: after Move up or Move down focus stays on the row moved, on whichever of the two buttons still works; a number not stored (offline, refused) goes back to the stored one, and the blur after Enter does not send it twice; the strip's round sits outside its list, so the list holds only its cards. Low, kept and recorded here: `enemies_seen` stays set when the reveal that set it is undone, since it says the encounter has had an enemy, not that one is up, and the end-combat prompt's Continue passes it; two DM browsers pressing Next at once pass two turns, last write wins as for every live command (`04` §2), and Previous takes one back.
payload.why: The owner's rule passes over an empty Enemies entry that never had a member (Q-106), whatever moved the turn there; and what players receive must follow from what they see (`04` §4), which an unseen turn's Next did not.
payload.alternatives: Keeping the turn's index after a removal (rejected: it could land on an entry that must be passed over); an expected-turn guard on Next and Previous (rejected for now: no other live command carries one, and Previous undoes a double press); undoing `enemies_seen` with the reveal (rejected: the flag records the encounter's history, not a token's state).

payload.title: TBL-06: test data directories start from a copy of a database migrated once per test process
payload.decision: `createTestData` (`server/src/http/testing/app.ts`) migrates one template database per test process with the real migrations and copies it into each test's data directory, then runs `migrateDataDirectory` on the copy, which finds nothing to apply; as `src/db/schema.test.ts` already does for its own fixture. Locally the server suite drops from 165 s to 111 s with the same 773 tests.
payload.why: On PR #31 `test · windows` failed three times on setup hooks and tests timing out at 60 s in files TBL-06 does not touch (ruler, camera, live, tokens, assets), the job taking 12 and 16.5 minutes against 8 on `main`. Each test data directory was migrated afresh, one committed transaction per migration, about 0.3 s a directory here and far more on the Windows runner; migration 0008 and TBL-06's new live tests added to every one of hundreds of such setups. Removing the cost at its cause is what the CI flake rule asks, not a longer timeout.
payload.alternatives: Raising the hook and test timeouts (rejected: hides the cost); fewer Vitest workers on Windows (rejected: slower everywhere for the same work); sharing one harness across the encounter tests alone (rejected: removes a fraction of the cost and weakens isolation).

payload.title: A Windows package before the release
payload.source: The owner, in chat on 2026-10-02: «How i could prepare it for shiping and deploying it in windows operational system as a package (in order to be as simple the installation). We are talking for self-hosting in a laptop or pc.» and «I wouldn't wanted to be hard to install to make it easy for the DM.» `09` §1 and `12` say the MVP is installed from source with Node and nothing is published (Q-017); `02` §8 and `12` say no packaging work is done in the MVP (Q-049); `01` §5 places a desktop wrapper in Phase 3.
payload.question: Is a Windows package that needs no Node or Git on the DM's PC built before the release, overriding Q-017 and Q-049?
options: A) A Windows x64 installer and a portable zip, each carrying its own Node runtime, the built server and client and the Windows binaries of better-sqlite3 and sharp, built by CI on a version tag and attached to a GitHub Release; started from a Start Menu shortcut that opens the DM view in the default browser; no Electron or Tauri window, no auto-update → effect on scope: a new Phase 6 with three packages; installation from source stays supported; Linux and macOS stay source-only.
B) The portable zip only, no installer → effect on scope: one package; the DM unzips and double-clicks, and allows the firewall prompt by hand.
C) Keep installation from source only → effect on scope: no change; a DM installs Node 24 and runs `npm install` and `npm start` as `09` §1 says.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner asked for an installation as simple as possible for a DM who is not a developer, and the zip falls out of the same build as a first step.

payload.title: Installing for every user with a firewall rule, or for one user without administrator rights
payload.source: `09` §4: on Windows the firewall asks on first start, and the README explains allowing Node on private networks only (Q-076). An installer can instead add the rule itself, which needs administrator rights. The TV reaches the server only through that rule (`02` §2).
payload.question: Does the Windows installer run with administrator rights to install for every user and add a private-profile firewall rule for the bundled runtime?
options: A) Yes: per-machine install under Program Files; the installer adds an inbound rule for the bundled executable on the private profile only, and the uninstaller removes it → effect on security: one UAC prompt at install; no firewall dialog at first start; never open on public networks; the data directory stays per user (`09` §5).

B) No: per-user install under the user's programs folder, no administrator rights; Windows shows its firewall dialog at first start and the README tells the DM to tick private networks only → effect on security: no elevated step at all; the DM can still allow public networks by mistake, as with a source install today.
payload.recommendation: A, because the firewall dialog is the step a DM most often gets wrong, and a private-only rule the installer writes is narrower than what a hurried click allows.

payload.title: Signing the Windows package
payload.source: An unsigned Windows installer or executable downloaded from the web is stopped by Microsoft Defender SmartScreen («Windows protected your PC») until the DM chooses More info, then Run anyway. Signing needs a certificate from a paid service, such as Azure Trusted Signing (a monthly fee) or an OV certificate.
payload.question: Is the Windows package signed for the release?
options: A) Unsigned for the first release; the README and the release notes show the SmartScreen screen and the two clicks past it, and give the SHA-256 of each file → effect on external: no cost and no account; the DM sees a warning once per downloaded file.

B) Signed through a paid signing service from CI → effect on external: a recurring cost, an identity verification of the owner and a secret in CI; no SmartScreen block once the publisher has reputation.
payload.recommendation: A, because the project is free and self-hosted for a known table, and signing can be added later without changing the package.

payload.title: PKG: a Windows x64 package with its own Node runtime, a portable zip and an installer, built by CI on a version tag
payload.decision: Draft, on the recommendations of Q-107, Q-108 and Q-109, none answered yet. A new Phase 6 in `13` with three packages. PKG-01 Portable build: the server bundled by esbuild into one module with `better-sqlite3` and `sharp` left external, so the `@emberglass/shared` workspace link is not shipped; a staged folder `Emberglass/` holding the Node 24 LTS `node.exe` renamed `emberglass.exe` with its icon and description set, `app/server.mjs`, `app/migrations/`, `app/client/dist/` and `app/node_modules/` with only the production native modules and their win32-x64 binaries, installed by `npm ci --omit=dev` on a Windows runner and never cross-built; `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` (Node, libvips under LGPL-3.0, every bundled npm licence) and a README naming the exact source tag (AGPL-3.0 §6); a launcher that, when `/api/health` already answers on the port, only opens `http://localhost:3000/dm` in the default browser, and otherwise starts the server and then opens it, so that PIN setup from loopback (`07` §1) works on the first run; the console window stays open and shows the TV address and QR code (`08` §9), and closing it stops the server. `paths.ts` resolves the migrations and the client from the bundle's directory. A real version replaces `0.0.0` in every `package.json` and is shown in About & credits. The zip and its SHA-256 are built by a `release` workflow on a `v*` tag on `windows-latest` and attached to a GitHub Release, which is not a package registry. PKG-02 Installer: Inno Setup over the PKG-01 folder; per-machine under Program Files with one UAC prompt (Q-108 A); Start Menu and optional desktop shortcuts; an inbound firewall rule for `emberglass.exe` on the private profile only, removed on uninstall; upgrade in place over an older version, the start-up migration and its dated backup doing the rest (`09` §2); uninstall never deletes `%APPDATA%\Emberglass` (`09` §5); unsigned, with the SmartScreen steps and the checksums in the README and release notes (Q-109 A). PKG-03 Package gates: the Windows CI job installs the built installer silently into a clean folder on the runner, starts the packaged launcher with an empty temporary data directory, and runs the five journeys of `10` §5, the hidden-information suite and the offline run against it (`10` §3, `10` §6); uninstalls and checks the data directory is still there; and a manual run in Windows Sandbox with no Node installed is recorded in `docs/acceptance/`. Nothing in the server's behaviour, the contract, the schema or the data directory changes: same process, same port, same `EMBERGLASS_PORT` and `EMBERGLASS_DATA_DIR`. No auto-update and no update check (`02` §6). Installation from source (`09` §1) stays supported and documented. Linux and macOS packages are not built. Rollback: delete the release assets and the workflow; nothing else depends on them.
payload.why: The owner wants a DM who is not a developer to install Emberglass without Node, Git or a terminal (Q-107). The architecture already fits: one Node process, no database server, state in one per-user directory, migrations with a backup at start, so the package only has to carry the runtime. Building on a Windows runner is the only way to get the right native binaries of `better-sqlite3` and `sharp`. A browser rather than a desktop window keeps the DM view and the TV exactly what the acceptance suite already tests, and `02` §8 still holds: a Tauri or Electron wrapper later can reuse the PKG-01 folder.
payload.alternatives: Electron (rejected for now: about 150 MB more and a second shell to maintain, for a window the browser already gives); Tauri (rejected: the server is Node, so Node still ships as a sidecar and Rust is added); a Node single executable application (rejected: native `.node` addons cannot load from inside it and would be extracted to disk at start, fragile with `sharp`); a Windows service (rejected: the data directory is per user and the DM starts the server when they play); MSI through WiX (rejected for now: more ceremony than Inno Setup for the same result; Inno Setup is free and scriptable from CI); per-user install without a firewall rule (Q-108 B); signing (Q-109 B, deferred).
payload.affected_specs: `01` §5, §8; `02` §8; `09` §1, §3, §4; `10` §4; `11`; `12`; `13` new §11 Phase 6; AGENTS.md architecture and commands

payload.title: Q-107 to Q-109 written into the specs: Phase 6, a Windows package before the release
payload.decision: The owner answered A to Q-107, Q-108 and Q-109 and approved D-164 on 2026-10-02, so D-164's draft holds as written. Amended by `make unlock`: `01` §5 (the Windows package is built before the release instead of a Phase 3 wrapper) and §8 (installer and zip on a GitHub Release, unsigned); `02` §8 (no packaging in the MVP; the package changes neither server, contract, schema nor data directory); `09` §1 (installable without Node from an installer or zip; the launcher opens the DM view on loopback; per-machine install, upgrade in place, data kept on uninstall; licences and source tag; no self-update), §3 (only Windows x64 packaged) and §4 (a private-profile firewall rule added and removed by the installer; the README warns about Public networks); `10` §4 (the package passes the acceptance scenarios, the hidden-information suite and the offline run once installed, and once by hand without Node); `11` a row before the release; `12` three register bullets; `13` §2 Phase 6 in the dependency graph and new §11 with PKG-01 to PKG-03 and their derived characteristics. Q-017 and Q-049 are not superseded: installation from source and the MVP's freedom from packaging both still hold, as Q-104 left the Phase 2 placement of `01` §4 standing for what it did not move.
payload.why: Q-107 asks for the package before the release; a card is resolved only once its answer is in the specs with its tag (`specs/README.md` §Provenance), and the release gate of `13` §1 needs the package's phase and acceptance to exist.
payload.alternatives: Superseding Q-017 and Q-049 (rejected: their statements stay true, the package is an addition beside them); placing the packages in Phase 4 (rejected: Phase 4 is done and its evidence recorded); amending `08` for the launcher (rejected: the launcher opens the existing DM view and adds no screen).

payload.title: PKG-01: how the portable package is built, launched, checked and released
payload.decision: Within D-164. `make package` (a new target of the command contract) runs `scripts/package/build.mjs` then `scripts/package/check.mjs`. The build: `npm run build` (external-URL check included), then esbuild bundles `server/src/main.ts`, `launcher-main.ts` and `auth/reset-pin-cli.ts` into `app/server.mjs`, `app/launcher.mjs` and `app/reset-pin.mjs`, ES modules with `better-sqlite3` and `sharp` external, `vite` and `@fastify/middie` (development only) external, `__EMBERGLASS_BUNDLE__` defined so that `paths.ts` finds `app/migrations/` and `app/client/dist/` beside the bundle, and a `createRequire` banner for the CommonJS libraries. The native modules are copied from the runner's own `npm ci` install with their production closure read from package-lock.json, keeping only the optional packages whose `os`, `cpu` and `libc` (read from the installed manifest, which the lock leaves out) fit the machine, and pruning better-sqlite3 to its `lib/` and this system's prebuilt binary. The runtime is the Node that runs the build (setup-node's from `.nvmrc` in CI), copied as `emberglass.exe` with its icon (from `client/public/favicon.svg`) and version strings set by resedit, its Authenticode signature dropped (unsigned, Q-109). `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` holds Node's LICENSE, then every npm package the server bundle's metafile names, the client's and shared's production closure and the shipped modules, each with its licence files; libvips' libraries are listed from a vendored copy of the sharp-libvips 1.3.3 table, which the build refuses for another libvips version, and the LGPL-3.0, GPL-3.0 and MPL-2.0 texts are vendored. `README.txt` names the tag and commit and the source URL (package.json `repository`). The zip is written by a small deflate writer in `scripts/package/lib.mjs` (no zip tool on the runner's PATH is relied on) with the commit's time, beside a `sha256sum`-format `.sha256`. The launcher is `Emberglass.cmd` running `emberglass.exe app\launcher.mjs`: it asks `GET /api/auth` on 127.0.0.1 and, on a 200 with a boolean `dm`, only opens `http://localhost:<port>/dm` (rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler, no shell) and exits; otherwise it imports `server.mjs` in its own process, so the window is the console of `09` §2 and closing it stops the server, then opens the DM view; a browser that cannot be started is replaced by the address printed. `Reset PIN.cmd` runs `app\reset-pin.mjs`: the package's form of the command of `07` §1, `npm run reset-pin` staying the source install's. The check unzips with Expand-Archive on Windows, runs the launcher with only the system folders on PATH (no Node, checked) and an empty `EMBERGLASS_DATA_DIR` on a free port, and requires `make smoke`'s checks, the data directory's files, the console's lines, a second launch that exits 0 having found the server and started none, the PIN reset, the exe's FileDescription and the shipped files. CI gains a `package · windows` job outside the gate matrix (only Windows is packaged), keeping the zip seven days; `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs the same target on a `v*` tag in a job with a read-only token, and a second Ubuntu job, which runs no project code, verifies the checksum and creates the GitHub Release as a draft (a pre-release for a tag with a suffix) until PKG-03's gates run before it. Off Windows the same target builds and checks the folder for that system (`emberglass.sh`), to try it locally; nothing publishes it.
payload.why: D-164 and PLAN named `/api/health`, but every `/api` route except `/api/auth` and `/api/setup` requires a DM session (`02` §5, Q-046, locked) and `app.test.ts` asserts `/api/health` is a 401; `/api/auth` is the unauthenticated route that already says a server is Emberglass, so no route is added and the register is kept. Copying the closure from the runner's `npm ci` gives the same Windows binaries as a second `npm ci --omit=dev` (D-164's wording) without a second lockfile to keep in step, and is what the substance of D-164 asks: built on Windows, never cross-built. Using the runner's Node avoids any download at build time and is exactly the `.nvmrc` version the tests ran on. The firewall prompt names a program by its FileDescription, so the exe has to say Emberglass for the README's instruction to match. Drafts keep an unchecked package from being published before PKG-03's gates exist (`13` §11 exit criteria); splitting the write token from the job that runs install scripts limits what a compromised dependency could do to the repository.
payload.alternatives: A public `/api/health` route (rejected: breaks Q-046, a locked decision, for nothing `/api/auth` does not already answer); probing `/api/health` and accepting its 401 (rejected: any server answering 401 would pass); `npm ci --omit=dev` in a staged folder with a derived lockfile (rejected: a second lockfile to keep in step for the same files); downloading Node from nodejs.org with SHASUMS256 verification (rejected for now: a network step for the version the runner already has); rcedit (rejected: runs a Windows binary, so needs Wine locally; resedit is plain JavaScript); bsdtar or Compress-Archive to zip (rejected: platform-specific, and the check already reads the zip with Expand-Archive); a published release from PKG-01 (rejected: the gates of PKG-03 must pass first); one release job holding `contents: write` (rejected: the install scripts of every dependency would run beside the token); adding `package` to the Windows gate matrix (rejected: `ci-consistency.test.mjs` requires identical matrices, and Linux is not packaged); amending `07` §1 to name `Reset PIN.cmd` (rejected: the MUST is a command on the server machine, which it is; D-028 names the source install's).

payload.title: PKG-01: version 1.0.0 in every package.json, the build's version shown in About & credits, and a tag that must name it
payload.decision: Every package.json (root, `shared`, `server`, `client`, `e2e`) and the workspace references to `@emberglass/shared` move from `0.0.0` to `1.0.0`, the version of the first release; the root package.json gains `repository` for the package's source offer. The client's Vite and Vitest configs define `__EMBERGLASS_VERSION__` from `client/build-version.ts`: the root version, or `EMBERGLASS_BUILD_VERSION` when a release build sets it from its tag, accepted only as that version or that version with a pre-release suffix (`1.0.0-rc.1`), anything else failing the build. About & credits shows `Version <version>` (message `about.version`). The release workflow fails a tag that is neither `v<version>` nor `v<version>-<pre-release>`, so the published zip, its README and the About dialog all carry the tag's version.
payload.why: D-164 and PLAN ask for a real version in About & credits; the tag a release is built from must not drift from the version the package shows, and a release candidate needs its own name without a commit that edits five manifests.
payload.alternatives: 0.1.0 or 0.9.0 (rejected: the first release is the MVP's, and `01` §1 calls it done); the version served by the server over REST (rejected: a contract change for a string the build already knows); the tag alone, package.json left at 0.0.0 (rejected: a source build would show 0.0.0); bumping package.json for each release candidate (rejected: an edit of five manifests per candidate, for what a tag suffix says).

payload.title: Which LAN address the connect panel and the QR code use on a PC with virtual adapters
payload.source: The owner's first run of the Windows package (PKG-01, CI run 36982005130's zip) on 2026-10-02: on a Windows PC with WSL and VMware, the Connect a screen panel and the console highlighted and QR-encoded http://172.21.112.1:3000/ (vEthernet), listing 172.20.48.1, 192.168.186.1 and 192.168.36.1 (virtual adapters) before the Wi-Fi's 192.168.1.133; the phone could not open the highlighted address or scan the code, and worked once the owner typed the Wi-Fi address. `08` §5 [Q-053] highlights the first private-range address in the system's order; G-031 (deferred since LIV-03) predicted this. Preferring 192.168/16 would not help here: the VMware adapters are in it too.
payload.question: How should the server choose the address it highlights and encodes in the QR code when the PC has virtual network adapters?
options: A) Rank by adapter: addresses of adapters whose names mark them as virtual (vEthernet, Hyper-V, WSL, VMware, VirtualBox, Docker, docker0, br-, veth, virbr, vmnet, utun, tailscale, ZeroTier) go after the others, private-range first within each group; everything is still listed, and today's rule applies when only virtual adapters are left → effect on ux: the Wi-Fi or Ethernet address is highlighted on the owner's PC and on most PCs with WSL, Hyper-V, Docker or a VM, with no setup step; an adapter named in a way the list does not know can still win, and the DM then types one from the list as today. No stored data, no contract change.

B) A, plus the DM can pick the highlighted address in the Connect a screen panel, the choice stored as a setting and used by the panel, the QR code and the console while that address exists → effect on ux and data: the DM can always correct a wrong guess in one click and the TV's address stays put between sessions; adds a settings field (a migration), a field in the settings contract and a control in the panel.

C) Keep Q-053 and document it: the console, the panel and both READMEs tell the DM that with WSL, a VM or a VPN the highlighted address may be wrong and to try the Wi-Fi one from the list → effect on ux: no code change; every DM with such a PC meets a QR code that does not open, as the owner did, and has to work out which address is the Wi-Fi.
payload.recommendation: A, because it fixes the case the owner hit and the common ones with no stored setting and no contract change, and B's picker can be added later if a DM still meets a wrong guess.

payload.answer: B, with A as the way it works by default: the server ranks the addresses by adapter so that the right one is highlighted with no chore for the DM, and a TV address chosen in Settings from the detected addresses, with their adapter names, is the emergency correction for a PC where the ranking guesses wrong, falling back to the automatic choice when the chosen address is gone

payload.title: Q-110 written into the specs: the TV address ranked by adapter, a TV address chosen in Settings as the emergency correction, Q-053 superseded
payload.decision: The owner answered Q-110 on 2026-10-02: B, with A as the way it works by default, the Settings choice being the emergency correction and not the preferred way. Q-053 is superseded by Q-110 (`card-superseded`). Amended by `make unlock`: `08` §5 (every address listed with its adapter's name; the prominent one, which the QR code encodes, chosen with no step by the DM, virtual adapters' addresses after the others and private-range ones first within each group; a TV address the DM may choose in Settings from the detected addresses, Automatic by default, falling back to automatic, with the panel and the console saying so, when the PC no longer has it); `09` §7 (the TV address is a setting changed without restarting); `03` §1 (Settings gains the TV address, an IPv4 address or none for Automatic); `02` §5 (`/api/settings` carries the TV address); `11` a row before the release; `12` the Q-053 bullet replaced by a Q-110 one; `13` §11 PKG-01 carries the change, its Surfaces derived again (data, ux added) and its Contract change now yes.
payload.why: The owner's first run of the Windows package highlighted and QR-encoded a WSL vEthernet address on a PC with WSL and VMware, so the phone could not open it; a card is resolved only once its answer is in the specs with its tag (`specs/README.md` §Provenance).
payload.alternatives: A alone (rejected by the owner: a guess from adapter names needs a way out when it is wrong); B with a free-text address field (rejected: a typed address may be the router, the DNS server or another PC, and the TV would get a dead QR code; the detected addresses with their adapter names say which is the Wi-Fi); the choice in the Connect a screen panel rather than Settings (rejected by the owner, who asked for Settings); keeping Q-053 and documenting it (option C, rejected).

payload.title: PKG-01, Q-110: how addresses are ranked by adapter name, and how the TV address is stored, served and chosen in Settings
payload.decision: `server/src/connect.ts` names each address with the key `os.networkInterfaces()` gives it (on Windows the connection's name, such as `Wi-Fi` or `vEthernet (WSL)`) and marks it virtual when that name matches one list: vEthernet, Hyper-V, WSL, VMware, vmnet, VirtualBox, vboxnet, host-only, Parallels, Docker, the Linux `br-`, `veth`, `virbr`, `lxc`, `lxd`, `cni`, `flannel` and `podman` prefixes, `utun`, `tun`, `tap` and `wg` with a number, WireGuard, Tailscale, ZeroTier (`zt`), Hamachi, NordLynx, OpenVPN, `vpn`, loopback and Npcap. The addresses are sorted, stably so that equals keep the system's order, by one rank: the chosen TV address first, then other adapters before virtual ones, a private-range address first within each. Settings gains `tv_address` (migration 0009, an additive nullable column whose CHECK keeps out anything but four dotted numbers; the contract's `Ipv4Schema` checks each part is 0 to 255), written by `PATCH /api/settings` as an address or null for Automatic and logged by name like the other settings. `GET /api/connect` reads it at each request and answers each address's `adapter` and `virtual`, the `chosen` address, `chosen_found`, and `automatic`, the address picked with no choice, which the Settings dialog names beside Automatic. The console at start ranks with the stored address, names each address's adapter, says when the chosen one is gone, and tells the DM to choose the TV address in Settings when the TV cannot open the first; its firewall line names Emberglass as well as Node.js. In the DM view the Settings dialog has a TV address select under the ruler rule: Automatic (recommended), with the address it picks now, then each detected address with its adapter, then a saved address the PC no longer has, marked, or neutrally named when the addresses could not be read; only a change is sent. Connect a screen shows the first address's adapter, says when it was chosen in Settings, names each other address's adapter, and warns when the chosen address is gone. Nothing of it reaches the players room: settings are never projected to players, and a test listens to a player socket through a change.
payload.why: Q-110 answered B with A as the default: the ranking must get the owner's PC right with no step (it puts Wi-Fi before vEthernet (WSL), vEthernet (Default Switch) and two VMware adapters), and the Settings choice is the way out when a name fools it. Adapter names are all Node gives without native code or a shell command; a select of the detected addresses keeps a typo, the router or the DNS server out of the QR code; stored in the settings row, the choice survives a restart as the TV's address should.
payload.alternatives: Ranking by the default route or gateway (rejected: Node does not expose routes, so it would need `route print`, `ip route` or a native module, platform by platform); preferring 192.168/16 then 10/8 then 172.16/12 (rejected: the owner's VMware adapters are 192.168 addresses); excluding virtual adapters' addresses from the list (rejected: `08` §5 lists every address, and a TV on a VM's network may need one); a free-text field (rejected in D-168); keeping the choice in memory only (rejected: it would be lost at each restart, and the console at start could never use it); a client-side guess of the automatic address (rejected: a chosen address that ties with the winner would be mislabelled; the server answers `automatic`).

payload.title: PKG-01 review fixes: the launcher on a taken port, the DM view on 127.0.0.1, Settings fitting laptop windows, honest isolation and package checks
payload.decision: The owner approved every medium and low finding of the PKG-01 review (2026-10-02) but three deferred as gaps. Launcher: it opens `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dm`, the address its probe asks, which `isServerMachine` accepts for PIN setup; on `EADDRINUSE` it asks again every half second for ten seconds and opens the DM view of an Emberglass that took the port first (two double-clicks), else it fails with `PortInUseError` and prints the port, and how to start on the next one (`set EMBERGLASS_PORT=…` then `Emberglass.cmd` in a cmd opened from the folder); a launch that only opened a running server exits 0, or 2 when no browser opened, so that the window stays. `Emberglass.cmd` and `Reset PIN.cmd` start with `setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion`, keep the program's exit code through `pause` and pause on any non-zero code. Connect a screen: one message per state for the adapter line, a status rather than an alert for a chosen address that is gone (with how to stop it), and a line that names the private network before the Settings correction; the console says `Connect a screen (<adapter>[, chosen in Settings]): …` and gives the same advice on every system. Ranking: within each group a link-local 169.254/16 address comes after other ones; the groups of `08` §5 are unchanged. Settings: the two field columns and the PIN column hold down to 941 px wide (the 1,200 px fallback to one field column made the dialog scroll at 620 px high), with `minmax(0, 1fr)` columns so a long adapter name does not widen one; shorter TV address hint; a saved address read without the detected ones is `<address> (saved)`. Package: README.txt and README.md give the SmartScreen step and the port note, README.txt names 127.0.0.1 and the port; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt lists Vite (whose helpers are in the client build) with its own licence only, and gives the MIT text with the author as holder to a package that declares MIT without a licence file. Tests: the firewall assertion of `connect.test.ts` restored whole; the players-room isolation moved to `ws/settings.test.ts` with a live scene, a players snapshot really sent and an acknowledged snapshot as the barrier; `tv_address` in `http/settings.test.ts` (logging, re-save, refusals beside valid fields); a real restart in `http/connect.test.ts`; the launcher's race, taken port, advice and a real `openInBrowser` failure; `window.spec.ts` at 1,200, 1,100, 1,024 and 960 × 620 (all four failing on the CSS before the fix); an e2e of the TV address against the real server; `ci-consistency` guarding the release's tag check. `check.mjs` unzips into `Emberglass (1) & Ünï Χάρτης`, quotes cmd as `/s /c ""…""`, checks a free port with a TCP connect, allows exactly this system's `@img` packages, proves the reset by setting the PIN again, restarts on the same data with a TV address this PC lacks, starts two launches at once, and launches on a port a plain HTTP server holds. The package jobs install `make` alone from MSYS2. Deferred: Connect a screen's height on a PC with five addresses (G-047), build provenance and duplicate drafts (G-048).
payload.why: Critical and high findings block merge and there were none; the owner asked for the rest to be fixed on the branch before merging. Opening the address the probe asked closes the window in which another local program on `[::1]` could stand in for Emberglass; the race and the taken port both ended in a raw Node error; the Settings regression at 941–1,200 px was the TV address field's; a test that could not fail and a loosened assertion are not evidence (`14` §3).
payload.alternatives: Listening on `::` as well as 0.0.0.0 (rejected for now: a change of the server's binding for every install, where opening 127.0.0.1 suffices for the launcher); failing at once on EADDRINUSE (rejected: two double-clicks are the common case); a single field column with the PIN change below at ≤1,200 px (rejected: taller than 620 px); ranking link-local addresses after virtual adapters' (rejected: `08` §5 puts every virtual adapter's address after the others; a spec change for a case with no private address at all); keeping the weak isolation test beside the strong one (rejected: its title claimed a snapshot check it did not make).

payload.title: 09 §1 amended: the package launcher opens the DM view at 127.0.0.1, the address it checks
payload.decision: Amended by `make unlock`, with the owner's approval on 2026-10-02: `09` §1's launcher statement names `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dm`, the loopback address the launcher asks whether a server answers on, instead of `http://localhost:<port>/dm`. Everything else in the statement, and its Q-107 tag, is unchanged: the DM view is opened on loopback, so PIN setup from the server PC (`07` §1) works on the first run. D-170 had already made the launcher open 127.0.0.1; this brings the spec in line with it.
payload.why: The PKG-01 security review (S-L1) found that the launcher checked 127.0.0.1 but opened `localhost`, while the server listens on IPv4 only: a browser resolving `localhost` to `::1` first could reach another local program holding the port there and show a fake DM page. D-170 fixed the code beyond what the spec said; a statement and its code must agree (`14` §10).
payload.alternatives: Reverting the launcher to `localhost` and keeping the residual as a gap (rejected by the owner); listening on `::` as well, so `localhost` resolves to Emberglass either way (rejected for now: it changes every install's binding for a launcher concern); `localhost` with a check of both loopback addresses (rejected: a check cannot stop the browser choosing the other one). Side effect accepted: a browser signed in at `localhost:<port>` and one at `127.0.0.1:<port>` hold separate DM sessions.

payload.title: PKG-02: an Inno Setup installer over the PKG-01 folder, built by make package on Windows and installed, upgraded and uninstalled on the CI runner
payload.decision: Within D-164 and Q-108. `scripts/package/lib.mjs` `innoScript` writes the installer's script and `build.mjs` compiles it with the Inno Setup 6 that the `windows-latest` image carries (6.7.1 on Windows Server 2025; `ISCC` overrides the path; a Windows machine without it is told where to get it), giving `Emberglass-<version>-win-x64-setup.exe` and its `.sha256` beside the zip. The script: a fixed AppId (2ADC5081-636A-4E62-B504-5FBEC0D6EFD8, never to change, by which an upgrade finds the install); `PrivilegesRequired=admin` under `{autopf}\Emberglass`, 64-bit mode; `CloseApplications=yes` so that an upgrade closes a running Emberglass; `[InstallDelete]` of `{app}\app` so that nothing of an older app remains; the AGPL shown as an information page, never accepted; a Start Menu group (Emberglass and Reset the Emberglass PIN, both the `.cmd` launchers with emberglass.exe's icon so the console behaves as with the zip, and Uninstall Emberglass) and a desktop shortcut on request, unticked; one `netsh advfirewall` rule named Emberglass for `{app}\emberglass.exe`, inbound, allow, private profile, deleted before it is added so that an upgrade leaves one, and deleted by `[UninstallRun]`; a post-install Start Emberglass run as the original user and skipped when silent; nothing naming the data directory, so uninstall leaves `%APPDATA%\Emberglass`. `check.mjs` always checks the installer's checksum; where `EMBERGLASS_PACKAGE_SYSTEM_TESTS=1`, which only the `package · windows` jobs of CI and the release set, it installs silently and checks the program folder, the Start Menu shortcuts, no desktop one and exactly one rule (inbound, allow, Private, enabled, this emberglass.exe, read with Get-NetFirewallRule); writes a version-8 database into the DM's `%APPDATA%\Emberglass` by the migration files 0001 to 0008 with a setting changed, and a file into the app folder; installs again over it and checks one rule, that file gone and the database byte for byte unchanged; starts the installed Emberglass and checks the backup `emberglass-backup-*-v8.db`, the setting kept and the schema migrated; uninstalls silently and checks the program, the shortcuts and the rule gone and the database still there. It refuses to run where an Emberglass install or data directory already exists. The release workflow attaches the installer and its checksum beside the zip, in a draft with notes naming both, the SmartScreen step and the checksums. `09` §1's launcher URL is 127.0.0.1 (D-171).
payload.why: Q-108 answered A: every user, one administrator prompt, Start Menu shortcuts, a private-profile rule removed on uninstall, upgrade in place, the data never deleted (`09` §4, §5). Inno Setup was chosen in D-164. No earlier release exists to upgrade from, so the upgrade is the same installer over an install whose data an older schema left, which is what an upgrade must keep and migrate; the `[InstallDelete]` and the planted file show the older app's files go. Running the installer changes the machine it runs on, so it is opt-in and the CI runner, discarded after the job, is the only place that opts in.
payload.alternatives: Shortcuts to emberglass.exe with launcher.mjs as an argument (rejected: a start-up failure would close the console before the DM could read it; the `.cmd` pauses); a rule per port rather than per program (rejected: `09` §4 names the executable, and a changed EMBERGLASS_PORT would need another rule); `netsh` without the delete before the add (rejected: an upgrade would leave two rules); Windows Firewall COM from Pascal code (rejected: more code for the same rule); deleting `%APPDATA%\Emberglass` on request in the uninstaller (rejected: `09` §5 says never); installing a pinned Inno Setup with Chocolatey (rejected for now: the image carries it; the build fails clearly if it goes); running the install checks wherever `make package` runs (rejected: it would install into a developer's Program Files and firewall); building an older installer from an older commit to upgrade from (rejected: no earlier commit has an installer).

payload.title: One server per data directory: a lock taken before migrations and clean-up, which the launcher treats as an Emberglass already starting
payload.decision: `server/src/db/lock.ts` takes the data directory for the process before `start()` migrates or cleans anything: an exclusive SQLite transaction (`BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`, no busy wait) on `emberglass.lock` in the data directory, held while the server runs and released on close; the operating system drops it when the process ends, however it ends. A second server on the same data directory, on any port, throws `DataDirectoryInUseError` (code `EMBERGLASS_DATA_DIR_IN_USE`, naming the directory) and starts, migrates and deletes nothing. The launcher handles it like `EADDRINUSE`: it waits up to ten seconds for an Emberglass that answers and opens its DM view, and otherwise shows the error. `npm run reset-pin` and `make migrate` take no lock: the PIN reset is meant to run beside a server (`07` §1). The package check starts a second server on another port beside a running one and requires the refusal.
payload.why: CI run 37003661035: of two launches at once, the second's server got as far as `prepareImagesDir`, which empties `images/.incoming` and recreates it, and failed with EEXIST after the first had recreated it; the launcher recovered only from EADDRINUSE, so the window showed the error. Behind it was a data hazard: start-up removes the files of uploads in flight and every image nothing references, so a second server started during a session, by hand or by such a race, could delete an image the DM had just uploaded and not yet given to an asset (specs/03-domain-model.md §7, `09` §2). Taking the port first cannot fix it, as Fastify listens only once its routes and the data are ready.
payload.alternatives: `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` for `.incoming` only (rejected: hides the crash and leaves the deletions racing); a lock file created with `wx` and removed at exit (rejected: a crash leaves it behind, and the DM has to delete it by hand); a lock inside `emberglass.db` (rejected: an exclusive lock there would block the server's own connection); binding the port before anything else and handing it to Fastify (rejected: more code for a check the lock makes unnecessary); leaving the launcher's race window as it was (rejected: two double-clicks are common).

payload.title: 09 §4 amended: the installer also blocks Emberglass on public and domain networks
payload.decision: Amended by `make unlock`, with the owner's approval on 2026-10-02 after the PKG-02 review: `09` §4 gains a statement beside the private-profile rule.
