The installer also adds an inbound rule that blocks the package's executable on the public and domain profiles, so Windows asks nothing there and a hurried Allow cannot expose the server, and removes both rules on uninstall. It carries the Q-108 tag, whose intent (private networks only) it enforces. The allow rule's statement is unchanged.
payload.why: The UX, security and correctness passes of the PKG-02 review each found that with a private-only allow rule, Windows still prompts when Emberglass listens on a network classed as Public, pre-ticked for Public. An Allow there creates a public rule and serves the plain-HTTP DM view and PIN entry on that network (`07` §4, Q-076). A block rule on those profiles removes the prompt, and Windows lets a block override any allow, so the private-only promise holds whatever is clicked.
payload.alternatives: Keeping one rule and telling the DM in the READMEs to choose Cancel on that prompt (rejected by the owner: a hurried Allow stays possible); scoping the allow rule to `remoteip=localsubnet` (not instead: it does not stop the prompt on Public networks).

payload.title: PKG-02 review fixes: Program Files only, a TCP allow and a public block rule, Emberglass stopped before upgrades and uninstalls, a real version upgrade checked, and a lock that cannot be collected
payload.decision: The owner approved every finding of the PKG-02 review (2026-10-02). Installer (`innoScript`): `DisableDirPage=yes` and `UsePreviousAppDir=no`, so the install folder is always `{autopf}\Emberglass`, whose permissions only administrators can change (S-H1). `x64os` only. The allow rule is `protocol=TCP` on the private profile. A second rule, 'Emberglass (blocked on public networks)', blocks the program on the public and domain profiles (D-174). Both are deleted before being added, and both are deleted on uninstall. `CloseApplications=force`, a `[Code]` `PrepareToInstall` and the first `[UninstallRun]` stop the `emberglass.exe` of this folder, and only that one, through PowerShell `Get-Process | Where-Object Path -eq | Stop-Process` (written without braces, which Inno Setup would read as constants). The first page is a short generated `installerInfo` text: what is installed, the firewall rules, where the data is and that it is kept, the PIN on first start, the AGPL in a line. `[Messages]` `ConfirmUninstall` and `UninstalledAll` say the data in %APPDATA%\Emberglass is kept. Build: where `EMBERGLASS_PACKAGE_SYSTEM_TESTS=1`, a second installer of the same folder labelled `0.9.0` goes into `dist/package/upgrade-test/`, which no upload names. Check (`installerChecks`): - installs 0.9.0 and checks each Start Menu shortcut's target through WScript.Shell, no desktop shortcut, and exactly one Uninstall registry entry under the fixed AppId at version 0.9.0; - checks exactly two inbound rules for this emberglass.exe, found by program path whatever their names (TCP allow Private, block Public and Domain); - seeds a version 8 database by the migration files named NNNN_*.sql, starts 0.9.0, and installs this version over it while it runs, with `/TASKS=desktopicon`; - checks that the running Emberglass was stopped, emberglass.exe replaced, one registry entry at the new version, the two rules, the old app file gone, the data unchanged, and the desktop shortcut; - starts it, and checks the v8 backup and that the schema equals the number of migrations; - uninstalls while it runs, with its exit code and `/LOG`, waiting until the whole program folder is gone, then checks that it stopped, the Start Menu folder and the desktop shortcut gone, no rule, no registry entry, and the data kept. In CI (`CI=true`) without `EMBERGLASS_PACKAGE_SYSTEM_TESTS=1` the check fails instead of skipping, and `ci-consistency.test.mjs` requires the variable, the four artifact globs in both package jobs, and the installer's checksum check and attachment in the release job (T-H1). Lock: every held lock stays in a module-level set until released, because `server.test.ts` showed an unreferenced better-sqlite3 connection is collected and its lock lets go. A damaged lock file (NOTADB, CORRUPT) is made again once. `DataDirectoryInUseError` says that Emberglass is running in another window, perhaps on another port, and what to do. The launcher waits up to 60 s for a server that holds the data directory, against 10 s for a taken port. `start()` takes an optional client folder and returns its port and a `close`. Tests: - `server.test.ts` runs the real `start()`. While another process (`--expose-gc`, its reference dropped and collected) holds the lock through `lockDataDirectory`, it checks the refusal and that an upload in flight, an unreferenced image, schema 8 and no backup are untouched. After that process is killed, it checks that the server starts, migrates, cleans and holds the lock, and that close releases it. A failed start must release it too. It fails without the module-level set. - `lock.test.ts` checks a refusal in under 500 ms and the remade lock file. - `launcher.test.ts` checks the 60 s wait, no browser and its own error. Messages: the launcher says to keep the window open, and the port advice names the folder and says it lasts for that start only. READMEs and README.txt cover both the installer and the zip (shortcuts, the Public-network setting, upgrading after the session, pinning to Start, one DM per shared PC, what a checksum proves). The release notes say which file to choose and show the certutil command with the real file name. Deferred: one user's launcher opening another user's server on a shared PC (G-049, documented).
payload.why: The review's highs: - a custom install folder can let any local user replace the program the firewall and Start Menu trust (S-H1); - the installer checks could be skipped silently in CI before a release (T-H1); - nothing proved the lock is taken before start-up touches the data (T-H2). Its mediums: - an upgrade or uninstall with Emberglass running had never been exercised; - the upgrade was not one between versions; - the rule allowed every protocol and left the Public prompt open; - the uninstaller's wording suggested the data goes. Writing `server.test.ts` found a real defect: a lock nothing refers to can be collected.
payload.alternatives: `[Dirs]` permissions on a custom folder (rejected: refusing other folders is simpler, and `09` §4 says Program Files); `taskkill /IM emberglass.exe` (rejected: it would also stop an Emberglass started from a zip elsewhere); `remoteip=localsubnet` on the allow rule (rejected for now: a TV on another subnet of a mesh network would be refused); a second ISCC run with a bumped AppVersion on every build (rejected: only where the installer checks run); a per-user marker so the launcher tells its own server from another user's (deferred by the owner, G-049).

payload.title: PKG-03: the package gates run against the installed package by make package-gates, in CI and before a release is published, with build provenance
payload.decision: Within D-164 and D-166. A new target of the command contract, `make package-gates` (`scripts/package/gates.mjs`), takes the package `make package` left in `dist/package/` and checks both files' `.sha256`. On Windows, only where `EMBERGLASS_PACKAGE_SYSTEM_TESTS=1`, it installs the installer silently into `C:\Program Files\Emberglass` (refusing where an install or `%APPDATA%\Emberglass` exists) and uninstalls it at the end. Elsewhere it unzips the zip into a temporary folder, so the gates can be run locally. It then runs, against that folder: the three `@gate:` tests of `10` §3 (`server/src/ws/hidden-information.test.ts`, and `player-command-rejection` and `image-revocation` in `commands.test.ts`) with `EMBERGLASS_TEST_PACKAGE`; and Playwright with `EMBERGLASS_E2E_PACKAGE`: the First run setup test, the five journeys of `10` §5 with the large-scene fixture and each browser's offline probe in every browser `EMBERGLASS_E2E_BROWSERS` names, and the offline gate last. It reads Vitest's and Playwright's JSON reports and fails unless each gate test, and each journey file in each browser, ran and passed. Every server of both runs is the package's own runtime (`emberglass.exe`, or `emberglass` off Windows) running its `app/launcher.mjs`, as `Emberglass.cmd` does, each on a fresh temporary data directory and a free port, with PATH set to an empty folder, so that no Node is found and the launcher opens no browser of its own; the e2e servers run under the offline guard (`--import`), and the offline gate requires, against a package, that every watched server was the package's launcher and none the source install's `start.mjs`. In package mode the WebSocket test harness (`server/src/ws/testing/harness.ts`) talks to the package over HTTP (`request` for a request without a session, which the gates now use in place of `app.inject`), reads the package's database through a read-only better-sqlite3 connection, and raises the test limits to 15 minutes, since a real server answers one snapshot request a second; the command-rejection gate also compares the versions its sockets' snapshots carry, which is all a package shows, beside the in-process counters it still checks. CI gains a `package gates · windows` job after `package · windows`, which downloads that job's `package-windows` artifact into `dist/package/` and runs `make package-gates` with `EMBERGLASS_E2E_BROWSERS=chromium,msedge`. The release workflow runs the same job after its package job, and its last job, `needs: [package, package-gates]`, runs no project code: it checks the checksums, attests the installer's and the zip's build provenance with `actions/attest` (pinned, v4.2.2; `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`), and publishes the release (a pre-release for a tag with a suffix) instead of drafting it. A draft an earlier attempt left for the tag is completed with `gh release upload --clobber` and `gh release edit --draft=false`; a release already published for the tag is refused, never replaced (G-048). The release notes name `gh attestation verify`. The manual install in Windows Sandbox is a run sheet, `docs/acceptance/pkg-03-sandbox-run.md`, for the owner.
payload.why: `10` §4 requires the Windows package to pass the acceptance scenarios, the hidden-information suite and the offline run once installed, before a release is published, and `13` §11's exit criterion is a release workflow that publishes only after the gates pass; D-166 left releases as drafts until then. Testing the artifact the package job built, downloaded as the release job downloads it, means the gates judge the bytes that are published. Running the launcher keeps D-164's 'starts the packaged launcher'; an empty PATH is a DM's PC without Node, and keeps the runner's own browser out of a run whose browsers must all go through the offline proxy. Reading the reports turns a test that was skipped, filtered away or run against the source tree into a failure rather than a pass. Opening the package's own database read-only lets the gates keep their database assertions without a test route in the product.
payload.alternatives: Starting `emberglass.exe app/server.mjs` instead of the launcher (rejected: D-164 names the launcher, and the server entry alone would not show the launcher starts it); letting the launcher open the runner's default browser (rejected: an unproxied browser beside the run, and one per server started); folding the gates into `make package`'s check (rejected: the package job would need Playwright's browsers and twice its time, and CI could not show which half failed); building the package again in the gates job (rejected: the gates would judge other bytes than those released); adding a test-only REST route for the database or the version counters (rejected: product surface for a test, and `02` §5 keeps every route behind the DM session); Firefox and WebKit in the package gates too (rejected for now: the server is what the package changes, the browsers' matrix already runs against the source install in `e2e · windows`, and Firefox's slow LAN loads on the runner (G-040) would only lengthen the job); keeping the release a draft for the owner to publish (rejected: `13` §11 asks the workflow to publish after the gates); replacing a published release's files on a re-run (rejected: its checksums are already out); `actions/attest-build-provenance` (rejected: since v4 a wrapper of `actions/attest`).

payload.title: PKG-03 review fixes: tested gate verdicts, fog revocation in the package gates, digests carried from the build, the release behind the owner's approval, and release notes that say what ran
payload.decision: The owner approved every finding of the PKG-03 review (2026-10-03, four passes: one high, the mediums and the lows) and chose to have publishing wait for their approval. Verdicts (T-H1, C-L2, C-L5): what `gates.mjs` requires of the Vitest and Playwright JSON reports moves into `scripts/package/lib.mjs` (`vitestVerdicts`, `playwrightVerdicts`, `browsersOf`, `journeySpecs`, `packagedServersVerdict`) with fixture-report tests in `lib.test.mjs` for a gate missing, skipped, failed, duplicated or renamed, a missing report, a journey missing in one browser, failed, flaky, skipped or passing only as an expected failure (`expectedStatus` must be 'passed'), nested suites and Windows paths, and the probe that carries the offline marker; a gate file holding `.fails(` fails every hidden-information gate; the journeys required are the spec files of `e2e/tests/journeys/` on disk. Where the gates ran (T-M1, C-L3): in package mode the harness appends one JSON line per packaged server to `EMBERGLASS_TEST_PACKAGE_LOG`, and `gates.mjs` requires at least four, every one naming the package's folder. Fog (C-M1, `10` §3): `@gate:image-revocation` now also paints fog over a visible token (its image refused) and erases it (granted again). Versions (T-M2): the command-rejection gate compares the versions its sockets' snapshots carry in both modes, and in process checks them against the counters before and after, in place of an assertion that was `[] == []` against a package. No browser (T-L1): the harness and the First run journey's own server require the launcher's 'Could not open a browser.' against a package; `e2e/package.ts` replaces every spelling of PATH, not only `PATH` (C-L4). `gates.mjs` stops at once when the installer fails, checks that `%APPDATA%\Emberglass` was never created, logs each gate's duration, lists every failed check at the end, and keeps the install inside its `try`; `global-teardown.ts` removes the empty PATH folder. Workflows (S-M1, S-M2, S-L2, C-M3, C-L1, T-M3): both package jobs output the SHA-256 of the installer and the zip; both gates jobs check the downloaded files against them before running, and the release job before anything else; the release job runs in a `release` environment, which the owner gives themselves as required reviewer, so a pushed tag builds and gates but publishes nothing until approved; it reads the release before attesting, refusing a published one, treating only gh's 'release not found' as none and failing on any other error; a draft an earlier attempt left is deleted and the release created afresh, so none of the draft's files rides along; `ci-consistency.test.mjs` requires all of this, and no `continue-on-error` or job-level `if:` on the gates or release jobs. Words (U-H1, U-M2, U-M3, U-M4, U-M5, U-L6, U-L7, S-L1, S-L3, S-L4): the README and the release notes say to check the checksum before opening a file and to stop on a mismatch, say again that a match does not show who built it, state exactly what the gates ran (the installer on a fresh Windows build machine: the hidden-information tests, the five DM journeys in Chrome and Edge, the offline check; the zip a start-up check), say the tests vouch for the program the workflow built, not its third-party packages, and present `gh attestation verify` as optional, with `--signer-workflow giorgosroussos/dnd-vtt/.github/workflows/release.yml`; the Sandbox run sheet stops on a checksum mismatch, gives `cd %USERPROFILE%\Downloads`, allows for no UAC prompt in Sandbox, asks for the firewall choice the README gives, records the PIN step after it is done, gives the Windows 11 Start path, and names virtualisation. The draft path is untested (G-050) and the environment's reviewer is the owner's to set (G-051).
payload.why: Critical and high findings block merge, and the owner asked for the rest to be fixed before merging. The gate script's verdicts are the release's gate and had been wrong once already, caught by hand; a check of the release's integrity must not rest on code nothing tests. `10` §3 names fog among the cases an image must be refused after, and `10` §4 asks for the suite once installed. A compromised test dependency in the gates job could otherwise replace the artifact the release job publishes and attests. Under D-166 a draft needed the owner's click; D-176 removed it, so anyone able to push a tag could publish. The notes claimed tests that had not run on the files they described.
payload.alternatives: Raising the verdict tests from the script by running it on fixture folders (rejected: minutes per case, and the install path only runs on Windows); keeping `JOURNEYS` as a list (rejected: a journey added later would not be required); proving the Vitest gates ran against the package by a marker in each test's output (rejected: harder to count than a file the script owns); checking only the release job's download against the digests (rejected: the gates would then not be known to have tested the built files); a tag ruleset limiting `v*` to the owner instead of the environment (rejected by the owner: the approval also stops a tag the owner pushed by mistake); keeping releases automatic (rejected by the owner); completing a leftover draft with `--clobber` (rejected: the draft's other files would be published with it); attesting after publishing (rejected: a file would be public before its provenance exists); a shorter per-test limit for package mode (rejected for now: the one-a-second snapshot throttle sets the floor; durations are logged instead).

payload.title: The Windows Sandbox install deferred: PKG-03 done without it, the manual install kept as gap G-046
payload.decision: Changes how the locked decision Q-107 (`specs/12-decision-register.md` §3, `10` §4: the Windows package passes the acceptance scenarios, the hidden-information suite and the offline run once installed before a release is published, and once by hand on a Windows with no Node installed) is met for this release: the automated half is done, the manual install on a Windows with no Node is deferred, not dropped. PKG-03 is marked done on what ran and passed: `make package-gates` and the `package gates · windows` job (D-176, D-177), green in CI run 37161252749, and the release workflow publishing `v1.0.0-rc.2` only after the gates and the owner's approval (run 37197305433), with both files' checksums and build provenance verified on download. The owner's own install of the downloaded `v1.0.0-rc.2` installer on their PC (2026-10-04) passed the short session, on a PC with an earlier install, so it is not the clean-Windows record. G-046 keeps the manual install in Windows Sandbox from a release candidate, with `docs/acceptance/pkg-03-sandbox-run.md` as the procedure, and any Mark-of-the-Web warning it finds still goes into the README, README.txt and the release notes. G-050 (a leftover draft release) and G-045 (the ruleset) stay open as they are. Spec text is unchanged; `10` §4 still requires the manual install, which is owed before the 1.0.0 release.
payload.why: Owner's decision on 2026-10-04: the owner does not want to run the Sandbox test now and asked to close the pull request and continue. Everything the repository can test without the owner's machine has run and passed, on the Windows runner and on the published pre-release.
payload.alternatives: Keeping PKG-03 in progress and the pull request open until the Sandbox run (offered to the owner, not chosen); counting the owner's own-PC install as the manual run (rejected: that PC had an earlier install and its data, and `10` §4 names a Windows with no Node); amending `10` §4 to drop the manual install (rejected: the owner defers it, and a locked decision is not rewritten by a deferral).

payload.title: The package and its gates run in CI on pushes to main and on demand, not on pull requests; G-045 retired
payload.decision: The owner's choice (2026-10-04): in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` the `package · windows` job carries `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so it and `package gates · windows`, which needs it and has no condition of its own, run on every push to `main` and on `workflow_dispatch`, never on a pull request. The release workflow is unchanged: on a tag it always builds, gates and waits for the owner's approval before publishing (D-176, D-177). `scripts/ci-consistency.test.mjs` requires the condition on the CI package job, the gates job's `needs: package`, CI's three triggers, and no condition on the release workflow's package job. G-045 is retired: a job that does not run on pull requests cannot be a required check of the ruleset on `main`, so the package jobs are left out of it by design; README.md says so.
payload.why: The two Windows jobs take about 15 minutes of runner time on every pull request and have hung intermittently in `make package` (twice in about ten runs), holding pull requests back for what the release workflow checks anyway before anything is published. Running them on `main` still shows a change that breaks the package right after it merges, and before any tag.
payload.alternatives: On demand only (rejected by the owner: the release workflow would be the first automatic check, so a break could first show when releasing); on pull requests that touch packaging files only (rejected by the owner: needs a path-filter step, and a server change elsewhere could break the package unnoticed); keeping them on every pull request and adding them to the ruleset as G-045 asked (rejected by the owner: the time and the intermittent hang on every pull request).

payload.title: Per-enemy initiative replacing the one Enemies entry
payload.source: The owner's brief for the DM toolkit, 2026-10-04: «Every visible monster or NPC in the combat gets its own entry (`kind: "monster"`, `token_id`, optional initiative number), ordered like PC entries»; «The TV strip shows enemies by their token label, exactly like PCs (e.g. "Bandit 1"). Only tokens visible to players appear (existing visibility rule, `04`)»; «An encounter in progress at upgrade time has its DM entry expanded in place into one entry per member»; «Supersedes the "one DM entry / never reveal enemies on the TV" decisions (Q-104 to Q-106, D-160 to D-162)». `01` §4 and §9 keep per-monster initiative in Phase 2 and `04` §4 forbids any monster or npc in the players' encounter (Q-104).
payload.question: Does every visible monster and npc in combat get its own initiative entry, shown on the TV by its label, replacing the one Enemies entry?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: one entry per visible monster or npc token (`kind: monster`, `token_id`, an initiative number or none), sorted and dragged like player characters' entries; the strip names each by its token label, only for tokens players can see (`04` §4); an encounter in progress at upgrade has its Enemies entry expanded in place into one entry per member; the encounter stays one per scene in SQLite → effect on scope: per-monster initiative leaves Phase 2; Q-104, Q-105 and Q-106 and D-160 to D-162 are superseded; players see the labels of visible enemies in turn order, which they already see on the map.
B) Keep the one Enemies entry → effect on scope: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner decided it and approved superseding the earlier cards.

payload.title: Hit points and armour class on every token
payload.source: The owner's brief for the DM toolkit, 2026-10-04: «Fields `hp_current`, `hp_max`, `hp_temp`, `ac`, all nullable. The DM may fill them for any token, PCs included»; «Asset gets optional default `hp_max` and `ac`, copied to new tokens»; «DM-only: never in any player snapshot or event»; «Automation only when `hp_max` is set: Bloodied on at hp_current ≤ hp_max / 2 (rounded down), off above it; at 0 HP a monster/NPC becomes Dead, a PC becomes Unconscious. Temp HP absorbs damage first»; «Moves "hit points" out of Phase 2 in `01`». `01` §1 puts no game rules in code, `01` §4 keeps hit points in Phase 2, and `04` §2 fixes the live token commands.
payload.question: Do tokens carry optional hit points and armour class, DM-only, with Bloodied, Dead and Unconscious set from the hit points?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: four nullable fields on every token, optional `hp_max` and `ac` defaults on the asset copied to new tokens, never sent to players; with `hp_max` set, Bloodied at or below half (rounded down) and off above it, Dead for a monster or npc and Unconscious for a player character at 0, temporary hit points taking damage first; set live by undoable token commands → effect on data: an additive migration on `token` and `asset`; hit points leave Phase 2; the automation is the one game rule in code beside the size table and the ruler.
B) Keep hit points in Phase 2 → effect on data: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner decided it.

payload.title: Follow my view: the TV camera mirroring the DM's
payload.source: The owner's brief for the DM toolkit, 2026-10-04: «A toggle on the live scene. While on, the player camera continuously mirrors the DM camera (throttled), fitting the DM's whole visible area inside the TV's aspect ratio, never cropping it»; «Turned off by Lock TV camera, by any manual TV camera control, or by switching the live scene»; «Amends `04` §9 (the reset-to-fit on activation still holds; follow starts off)». `04` §9 sets the player camera only by an explicit DM action.
payload.question: Is there a Follow my view toggle that keeps the TV camera on the DM's view?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: a toggle on the live scene, off at every activation; while on, the DM view sends its whole visible area as the player camera, throttled, widened to the TV's aspect ratio and never cropped; Lock TV camera, any manual TV camera control and a change of live scene turn it off → effect on ux: the TV follows the DM's pans and zooms without a click; no new command or stored state.
B) Keep the explicit Send my view only → effect on ux: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner decided it.

payload.title: DM notes per scene and per token
payload.source: The owner's brief for the DM toolkit, 2026-10-04: «A note per scene and a note per token. A token also shows its asset's `notes` read-only»; «DM-only, filtered on the server like hidden tokens»; «Moves "DM notes per scene" out of Phase 2 in `01`». `01` §4 keeps DM notes per scene in Phase 2; `04` §4 already keeps asset notes from players.
payload.question: Do scenes and tokens carry DM notes, kept from players on the server?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: a `notes` text on every scene and every token, the token's view also showing its asset's notes read-only; never in a player snapshot or event → effect on security: two more DM-only fields the players' projection must drop, covered by the hidden-information suite; DM notes per scene leave Phase 2.
B) Keep DM notes in Phase 2 → effect on security: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner decided it.

payload.title: Campaign and library export and import as a zip
payload.source: The owner's brief for the DM toolkit, 2026-10-04: «Two scopes: a whole campaign (with the assets and images it uses), or library assets (selected or all)»; «Zip with a versioned `manifest.json`, data as JSON, and images named by hash»; «A campaign always imports as a new copy with new ids. Images are deduplicated by hash, and assets with an existing id are reused»; «Reject newer format versions, oversized archives and paths that escape the target ("zip slip")»; «Supersedes Q-013 (copy the data folder) as the only way to move a campaign». `01` §4, `09` §5 and `12` keep export and import in Phase 2 (Q-013), and AGENTS.md lists it among the red lines.
payload.question: Can the DM export a campaign or library assets to a zip and import it on another Emberglass?
options: A) As the owner wrote it: a campaign with the assets and images it uses, or library assets (selected or all), exported as a zip holding a versioned `manifest.json`, the data as JSON and the images named by their sha256; a campaign always imported as a new copy with new identifiers, images deduplicated by hash, assets whose identifier exists reused; newer format versions, oversized archives and paths escaping the target refused → effect on scope: export and import leave Phase 2 and Q-013 is superseded; copying the data folder stays the backup.
B) Keep export and import in Phase 2 (Q-013) → effect on scope: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, because the owner decided it.

payload.title: Dead and Unconscious when hit points rise above 0
payload.source: Asked on 2026-10-04 while writing Q-112 into the specs: the owner's brief says what the automation sets at 0 hit points and that Bloodied goes off above half, but not whether healing above 0 takes Dead or Unconscious away.
payload.question: When a token's hit points rise above 0, does the automation clear the Dead or Unconscious it set at 0?
options: A) Clear Unconscious only; Dead is never cleared by the automation → effect on ux: a healed player character is up again without a click; a monster's Dead stays until the DM removes it.
B) Never clear either; the automation only sets them at 0 → effect on ux: the DM removes Dead or Unconscious by hand after healing.
C) Clear both → effect on ux: healing a token by mistake can bring a dead monster back on the TV.
payload.recommendation: A, because a healed player character is conscious by the rules, and a monster's death is the DM's call.

payload.title: A monster or npc that players first see after combat started
payload.source: Asked on 2026-10-04 while writing Q-111 into the specs: the brief gives every visible monster or npc an entry, but not what happens to one revealed mid-combat. `08` §12 already offers to add a player character players can now see.
payload.question: When a monster or npc token becomes visible to players during combat, does it get an entry automatically or is the DM offered to add it?
options: A) Offered, as player characters are: «Add Bandit 3 to initiative?», at the end of the order; nothing reaches the TV until the DM accepts → effect on ux: one click per late enemy; an enemy revealed for a moment never enters the order by accident.
B) Added automatically at the end of the order → effect on ux: no click; the strip shows it at once, also for a token revealed by mistake.
payload.recommendation: A, because it matches the offer the tracker already makes for player characters.

payload.title: A monster or npc entry whose token is Dead or unseen
payload.source: Asked on 2026-10-04 while writing Q-111 into the specs: with one entry per enemy, the brief does not say what happens to an entry whose token is marked Dead or that players can no longer see, nor what becomes of the «No enemies left. End combat?» prompt of Q-106.
payload.question: Is an entry whose monster or npc is Dead or unseen kept and passed over, or removed?
options: A) Kept, its turns passed over; the strip drops an unseen one and greys a Dead one; when no monster or npc entry can take a turn, once the encounter has had one, the DM is asked «No enemies left. End combat?» → effect on ux: undo and a mistaken Dead are easy to put right; the end-of-combat prompt survives.
B) Removed, undo bringing it back → effect on ux: the list shrinks as enemies fall; a revived enemy needs adding again.
payload.recommendation: A, because the entry keeps its place for a mistake put right, and the prompt the owner asked for in Q-106 keeps working.

payload.title: The size limit of an import archive
payload.source: Asked on 2026-10-04 while writing Q-115 into the specs: the brief rejects «oversized archives» without a size. The upload limit of `05` §6 is 50 MB by default, too small for a campaign with its maps.
payload.question: What limit decides that an import archive is oversized?
options: A) A setting of its own, 2 GB by default, applying to the archive and to the total of its entries once unpacked → effect on security: a zip bomb is refused before it fills the disk; the DM can raise it for a large campaign.
B) Fixed at 2 GB → effect on security: the same protection, no setting to change.
C) The upload limit → effect on security: most campaigns with maps are refused at the default.
payload.recommendation: A, because the DM can raise it without a new release, and the unpacked total is what protects the disk.

payload.title: The DM toolkit (Phase 7): hit points and armour class, per-enemy initiative, Follow my view, DM notes, export and import
payload.decision: The owner's decisions of 2026-10-04, recorded as cards Q-111 to Q-115 (each answered A) and the follow-ups Q-116 (B), Q-117 (A), Q-118 (A) and Q-119 (A). (1) Per-enemy initiative (Q-111, Q-117, Q-118): every visible monster or npc in combat gets its own entry `{ id, kind: 'monster', token_id, initiative }`, ordered like player characters' entries; the one Enemies entry and its computed members go; the TV strip shows each entry whose token players can see by its token's label, a Dead one greyed; an entry whose monster is Dead or unseen stays and is passed over; a monster or npc players first see mid-combat is offered to the DM, never added by itself; «No enemies left. End combat?» shows when no monster or npc entry can act once the encounter has had one; an encounter in progress at upgrade has its Enemies entry expanded in place into one entry per member. The encounter stays one per scene in its own table. Supersedes Q-104, Q-105 and Q-106 and D-160, D-161 and D-162: their storage (the `encounter` table of migration 0008), command set, `encounter.updated` event, undo through the whole encounter before, players' projection compared around every command, Initiative tab and strip carry over wherever `04` §14 and `08` §12 do not now say otherwise. (2) Hit points and armour class (Q-112, Q-116): nullable `hp_current`, `hp_max`, `hp_temp` and `ac` on every token, optional `hp_max` and `ac` defaults on the asset copied to new tokens; never sent to players; with `hp_max` set, Bloodied at or below half rounded down and off above it, at 0 Dead for a monster or npc and Unconscious for a player character, temporary hit points taking damage first; rising above 0 removes neither Dead nor Unconscious. This is the one game rule in code beside the size table and the ruler, an exception to `01` §1 and its register bullet. New live commands `token.setStats` and `token.adjustHp`, undoable, widen the locked set of live token commands. (3) Follow my view (Q-113): a toggle on the live scene, off at every activation, sending the DM's whole visible area as the player camera, throttled and widened to the TV's aspect ratio, never cropped; Lock TV camera, any other TV camera control or a change of live scene turns it off; no command or stored state is added. (4) DM notes (Q-114): a `notes` text on every scene and token, the token's asset's notes shown beside it read-only; filtered on the server like hidden tokens. (5) Export and import (Q-115, Q-119): a campaign with the assets and images it uses, or library assets selected or all, as a zip with a versioned `manifest.json`, JSON data and images named by sha256; a campaign always imports as a new copy with new identifiers, images deduplicated by hash, assets with an existing identifier reused; a newer format version, a path escaping the target, or an archive or unpacked total over the import limit (a new setting, 2 GB by default) is refused with nothing stored. Supersedes Q-013. Locked text changed: `12` §1 (entities' provenance; hit points, notes and export bullets), §2 (hit points and notes never reach players; import refusals), §3 (no game rules but the hit-point automation; export and import built; live token commands; the initiative bullets; Q-116 to Q-118), §5 (Follow my view); AGENTS.md red lines on hidden information, scope, preparation and play, and uploads. Phase 7 in `13` §12: DMT-01 hit points and armour class, DMT-02 per-enemy initiative, DMT-03 Follow my view, DMT-04 DM notes, DMT-05 export and import, in that order. Data migration plan (`09` §2, `14` §8): DMT-01 adds nullable columns to `token` and `asset`; DMT-04 adds `notes` to `scene` and `token`; DMT-05 adds the import limit to `settings`; all additive. DMT-02 rewrites each stored encounter's `entries` JSON in place, replacing the Enemies entry by the members it had at upgrade (monster and npc tokens players could see, without Dead), computed once in the migration's transaction; it is not reversible in place, since members were never stored, and its rollback is the dated copy of the database taken before migrations run (`09` §2). Its tests run on a generated fixture database (Q-082).
payload.why: The owner asked for these five changes in the brief of 2026-10-04 and decided each one, superseding the cards they overturn; the four follow-ups were asked of the owner on the same day because the brief left them open and each changes what the DM or the TV sees, or what the server accepts. Hit points come first because per-enemy initiative passes over a monster its hit points made Dead; export and import come last so that its format carries every field the others add.
payload.alternatives: Keeping the one Enemies entry and the strip that names no enemy (Q-104, rejected by the owner); hit points in Phase 2, or for monsters only (rejected by the owner: any token, player characters included); notes in Phase 2 (rejected by the owner); export and import in Phase 2 with the data folder copy as the only way to move a campaign (Q-013, rejected by the owner); merging an imported campaign into an existing one, or overwriting an asset whose identifier exists (rejected by the owner: always a new copy, existing assets reused); clearing Unconscious when hit points rise above 0 (recommended in Q-116, rejected by the owner); adding a late enemy automatically (Q-117) or removing a Dead or unseen enemy's entry (Q-118) (rejected by the owner); the upload limit or a fixed limit for imports (Q-119, rejected by the owner); storing the members of the old Enemies entry at upgrade time in a separate column to make the migration reversible (rejected: the dated backup already covers rollback, and the column would outlive its use).

payload.title: Q-111 to Q-119 written into the specs: Phase 7, the DM toolkit, with the defaults the owner's answers leave open
payload.decision: Writes D-180 into the specs by `make unlock` of `01`, `02`, `03`, `04`, `05`, `07`, `08`, `09`, `10`, `11`, `12` and `13`. `01` §1 gains the hit-point automation as the only other rule in code; §4 moves hit points, per-enemy initiative, DM notes per scene and export and import out of Phase 2; §9's tracker bullet is per enemy; new §10 lists the toolkit. `02` §5: notes at any time on `/api/scenes/:id`, defaults on `/api/assets`, the import limit on `/api/settings`, new `/api/export` and `/api/import`. `03` §1: the new fields on Asset, Scene, Token and Settings and the Encounter's `kind: monster` entries; §2 and §7 retagged, duplication copying hit points and notes; new §9 (hit points and armour class) and §10 (DM notes). `04` §2: `token.setStats` and `token.adjustHp`; §3: `token.updated` for hit points, `notes.updated` to the DM room only; §4: hit points, armour class and notes filtered on the server, the players' encounter carrying every entry of a token they can see; §8: the new commands undoable; §9: Follow my view; §14 rewritten per enemy, with the upgrade's expansion; new §15 (hit points) and §16 (DM notes). `05` §1 and §3: asset defaults, a token's own markers, hit points and notes. `07` §9: export and import behind the DM session, the refusals. `08` §12 per enemy; new §13 (the DM toolkit in the DM view). `09` §5 (moving a campaign by export), §7 (the import limit setting), new §9 (export and import). `10` §3: the hidden-information script with hit points, notes and enemy entries, and an export and import test. `11`: rows moved to the DM toolkit. `12`: as D-180 lists. `13` §2 and new §12: Phase 7, DMT-01 to DMT-05, with derived characteristics and per-package exit criteria. Every changed statement carries Q-111 to Q-119; the [Q-104], [Q-105], [Q-106] and [Q-013] tags moved to their successors. Defaults the owner's answers leave open, tagged [D-181] and each open to the owner: a token placed from an asset starts at that `hp_max` with no temporary hit points, and a later change of the asset's defaults changes no token (`03` §9); damage stops at 0, healing at `hp_max`, and healing adds no temporary hit points (`04` §15); the markers set by hit points are part of the same undoable step, an object token gains neither Dead nor Unconscious, and a Dead set this way passes a monster's entry over as any Dead does (`04` §15); notes are edited over REST on any scene, live included, not undoable, the DM room told by `notes.updated` (`04` §16); the expanded entries of an old Enemies entry take its initiative number and the token-list order, the turn passing to the first, an Enemies entry with no member removed (`04` §14); live state and settings are not exported, image variants are produced again on import, and an imported asset the server does not hold keeps its identifier (`09` §9). Within Q-111 the spec also says: `encounter.start` leaves out monsters and npcs already Dead, and `encounter.removeEntry` removes any entry. The command names `token.setStats`, `token.adjustHp` and the event `notes.updated` are this amendment's. Phase 7 is not added to the release gate: whether the DM toolkit ships before 1.0.0 is not decided here.
payload.why: A card is resolved only once its answer is in the specs with its tag (`specs/README.md` §Provenance), and Phase 7's packages need the sections they cite. The defaults are the smallest reading of the owner's words that an implementation needs; tagging them [D-181] rather than with the owner's cards keeps the record of what the owner said and what the agent filled in apart.
payload.alternatives: Opening a card for each default (rejected: each follows from the owner's answer, and the four that change what the DM or the TV sees were asked as Q-116 to Q-119); one live `token.setHp` command taking either new values or a delta (rejected: two commands with one meaning each are simpler to validate and to undo); notes as a live command with undo (rejected: notes never reach the TV, and a REST edit is how the DM edits any other prepared text); keeping the hit-point and notes fields out of `03` §1's table (rejected: the table is the list of stored fields); placing the toolkit in Phase 5 (rejected: Phase 5 is done and its evidence recorded).

payload.title: DMT-01: hit points and armour class stored, commanded, filtered for players and shown in the DM view; the command named token.applyHp
payload.decision: Within D-180 and D-181. Contract: `shared/src/hp.ts` holds the bounds (`hp_max` 1 to 9999, `hp_current` and `hp_temp` 0 to 9999, `ac` 0 to 99, each or null), the schemas and every rule, pure, which the server and the DM view's test server both apply: `statsFromAsset` (a new token at the asset's maximum, full, no temporary hit points), `withStats` (fields set or cleared; `hp_current` never above `hp_max`, so a lowered maximum brings it down; 0 temporary hit points stored as none), `applyHp` (a signed amount; damage takes temporary hit points first and stops at 0, healing stops at `hp_max` and adds no temporary hit points; none without current hit points), `markersForHp` (with both `hp_max` and `hp_current`: Bloodied at or below half rounded down and off above, kept at 0; at 0 Dead for a monster or npc, Unconscious for a player character, nothing for an object; never removes Dead or Unconscious, Q-116; new markers last), `parseHpEntry` (`-7`, `+5` or a bare number) and `compactHp` (`12/27`, `12+5/27`). `TokenSchema` and `AssetSchema` gain the fields, so the DM's tokens and assets carry them and `PlayerTokenSchema`, built field by field, does not. Commands: `token.setStats` (any of the four, at least one) and `token.applyHp { delta }` (the owner's name and shape, asked on 2026-10-04 against D-181's `token.adjustHp`; `04` §2 and §15 and `13` §12 amended by `make unlock`); `applyHp` on a token without current hit points is refused as `bad_request`, on a scene that is not live as `scene_not_live`, and a delta of 0 changes nothing. Storage: migration 0010 adds the four nullable columns to `token` and `hp_max` and `ac` to `asset`, each with a CHECK on its bounds; additive, rollback is the dated backup. `updateToken` sets the markers from the hit points whenever they change, inside its transaction, unless the same write gives the markers, which is how the undo and a REST body with markers put both back; armour class alone runs no rule. Undo: both commands' inverse is `token.restoreStats` (not on the wire), the four fields and the markers before, so one undo or redo takes back the markers too. Projection: a `token.updated` of a visible token whose only change is hit points or armour class reaches the DM's room only, so players' version counter cannot count it (`dmOnlyChange` in `server/src/ws/projection.ts`); a marker it set reaches them as any marker change. Preparation: `PATCH /api/tokens/:id` takes the four fields with the same rule; asset bodies take `hp_max` and `ac`, null clearing one. DM view: the popover's hit-point row (current / maximum, temporary hit points, a 4 px bar turning the Bloodied colour at half), the armour class on a shield, a click on either opening an in-place editor of maximum, temporary and armour class (empty clears; a maximum given to a token with none fills its current hit points), and one field taking `-7`, `+5` or a bare number on Enter, reached with D from anywhere a shortcut acts while a token is selected; in preparation the client applies `applyHp` and sends the resulting fields over REST. The "In this scene" rows and the Initiative rows, the Enemies members included, show the compact hit points and armour class; the asset editor has Default max HP and Default AC, sent only when set or changed. Kept as the specs say, the owner asked on 2026-10-04 against the brief for this package: healing from 0 removes neither Dead nor Unconscious (Q-116), and Bloodied stays on at 0 (`04` §15). Two tests that read the specs (`schema.test.ts`, `live.test.ts`) name the fields and event DMT-04 still has to build (`notes`, `notes.updated`), which that package removes from their lists.
payload.why: One pure rule set keeps the server and the DM view's tests in step, as the encounter's does (D-161). The rule in the write itself, not in the command, is what makes preparation, live commands, undo and redo agree. Filtering a hit-point-only change from players is required by `04` §4: an unchanged token sent to them would still move their version counter.
payload.alternatives: `token.adjustHp` with separate damage and healing amounts (D-181; replaced by the owner's `token.applyHp { delta }`); clearing Dead or Unconscious that the hit points set when healed above 0, and taking Bloodied off at 0 (the brief's wording; the owner kept Q-116 and the spec when asked); a players' event for every change of a visible token, as before (rejected: it leaks that the DM changed hit points); recording which markers the rule set, to remove only those later (rejected: no rule removes Dead or Unconscious, so nothing needs the record); refusing a current above the maximum instead of bringing it down (rejected: lowering a maximum would then take two commands); computing damage in the client on the live scene and sending `token.setStats` (rejected: two DM browsers damaging the same token would lose a hit, while the server applies each delta to what it holds).

payload.title: DMT-02: a late entry may carry its initiative number; the tokens players newly see offered together; Add to initiative in the popover and Remove dead
payload.decision: The owner's brief for DMT-02 (2026-10-04) asks for more than `04` §14 and `08` §12 said, and the specs now say it, by `make unlock` of both: (1) `encounter.addEntry` takes an optional `initiative`; with one, the entry goes before the first entry with a lower number or none, so after the entries with the same number, and the rest of the order stays as it stands, a drag included; without one, at the end as before (`04` §14). (2) The offer of Q-117 lists every token players can now see that has no entry in one prompt, each with an optional number field, with Add all and Skip ("Add {name} to initiative?" for one token); Skip adds none (`08` §12). (3) While combat runs, the token popover's menu has Add to initiative for a player character, monster or npc without an entry, disabled with its reason when players cannot see it or a monster carries Dead; each row has a remove action, and Remove dead beside the round removes every Dead monster's and npc's entry (`08` §12). Kept as the specs and Q-118 say, the owner asked on 2026-10-04 against the brief: a Dead monster players can see stays on the TV strip, greyed, rather than leaving it.
payload.why: The brief asks for each of these and nothing in the register forbids them; the number on a late entry spares the DM a drag after every reveal, and inserting by it rather than sorting the whole order keeps the order the DM dragged, which `04` §14 says stands until a number is set again. The owner was asked about the Dead strip card because the brief contradicted Q-118 and chose Q-118.
payload.alternatives: Re-sorting the whole order on a late entry's number, as setting a number does (rejected: it would undo a drag the DM made to break a tie); one offer per token, as before (rejected by the brief: a fog region revealing four goblins would stack four prompts); a new command for Remove dead or Add all, one undo step each (rejected: the brief keeps the command set; each entry removed or added is its own undoable command); leaving a Dead monster off the TV strip (the brief's wording; the owner kept Q-118).

payload.title: DMT-02: per-enemy initiative, the Enemies entry expanded by migration 0011 with a step in code, the TV strip naming each enemy by its label
payload.decision: Within D-180, D-181 and D-183. Contract (`shared/src/encounter.ts`): `MonsterEntrySchema` `{ id, kind: 'monster', token_id, initiative }` replaces `DmEntrySchema`, the union is `pc | monster`; `membersOf` is gone. `TurnView` is the ids players see and the ids carrying Dead; `takesTurn` takes a player character's entry while its token is seen, whatever it carries, and a monster's while seen and not Dead; `canEnter`, `entryKindOf`, `startTokens` (player characters and living monsters and npcs players see, in the token list's order) and `missingTokens` serve start, the offer and `addEntry`; `insertionIndex` places a numbered late entry. `enemies_seen` now records that a monster or npc entry could take its turn at some point of the encounter (a reading of `08` §12's "once the encounter has had one": an encounter that never had a monster entry, or only unseen ones, never asks), set by `notingEnemies` after every change as before; `noEnemiesLeft` is that flag with no monster entry able to act. `PlayerEncounterEntrySchema` is `{ id, kind: 'pc' | 'monster', token_id }`; the players' projection carries every entry whose token they see, a Dead monster's included (the strip greys it from the marker players already see), `current` and `next` indexing that list, neither named while the turn is on an entry they cannot see. Server: `dropEntriesOf` takes a deleted token's entry of either kind; `addEntry`'s optional number is passed through. Migration 0011 changes no schema: its SQL is a no-op and the expansion is a step in code that `server/src/db/migration-steps.ts` gives that file name, run by `migrate.ts` in the migration's transaction after the backup; it reads tokens, assets and fog with its own queries, so later schema changes do not break it, expands each Enemies entry in place by the members it had (D-181), shifts `current_index` by the entries added minus one when it pointed after it, passes an empty Enemies entry's turn to the next entry that takes it, a round more past the last, checks every result against `EncounterSchema` and fails the migration otherwise. DM view: monster rows like a player character's (avatar in the side's ring colour, number field, compact hit points and armour class, remove), a Dead monster's greyed with its skull among its markers, an unseen row dimmed with the hidden token styling; the Enemies row and its member list, and the map's member ring, are gone; the turn's token, a monster's too, is ringed and centred. "No enemies left. End combat?" shows when the turn changes while `noEnemiesLeft` holds, until answered or an enemy can act again; Continue only dismisses it, since nothing holds the turn any more. The offer is one prompt for all tokens offered; tokens skipped, or whose entry the DM removed, are not offered again in that browser. TV: each card shows its token's portrait and label in its category's ring colour (`--monster`, `--npc`), a Dead one greyed and struck through.
payload.why: One rule set shared by the server, the DM view's test server and the projection keeps the three in step, as D-161 did. A migration step in code is the only way to compute members, which depend on the fog; running it inside the numbered migration keeps the backup and the one-transaction rule of `09` §2, and keying it by file name keeps it from firing on a test's own migrations. Asking on a change of turn rather than holding the turn on an entry is what remains of Q-106's stop once no single entry stands for the enemies.
payload.alternatives: Expanding at start-up outside the migration runner (rejected: no backup is taken and the expansion would run on every start); computing members with `listTokens` (rejected: it reads the latest schema, which a later migration may change); keeping `enemies_seen` as "had a member" from the token list (rejected: with entries per enemy, a hidden or never-added monster must not arm the prompt); showing the prompt whenever no enemy can act (rejected: `08` §12 asks on Next); leaving a Dead monster off the strip (the brief's wording; the owner kept Q-118).

payload.title: Follow my view while the DM opens another scene to prepare
payload.source: Asked on 2026-10-05 while implementing DMT-03: `04` §9 and `08` §13 (Q-113) say what turns Follow my view off (Lock TV camera, another TV camera control, another scene going live, the TV going idle) but not what it does while the DM view shows a scene that is not live, where the DM's camera is not on the live scene's world.
payload.question: While Follow my view is on and the DM opens a non-live scene to prepare, what happens to it?
options: A) It pauses: nothing is sent and the TV stays where it was; on returning to the live scene it resumes and sends the DM's view at once; the live indicator says it is paused → effect on ux: the DM can prepare the next scene mid-session without the TV moving, and following picks up again without a click.
B) It turns off, like a manual TV camera control → effect on ux: the DM turns it on again after every look at another scene.
C) It keeps sending the last view of the live scene → effect on ux: nothing changes on the TV, but the toggle looks on while nothing follows.
payload.recommendation: A, because preparing the next scene is not a decision about the TV, and the TV should neither jump nor stop following because of it.

payload.title: DMT-03: Follow my view lives in the DM view, sent through a 100 ms throttle, the frame hidden while it is on, C as its shortcut, and the TV gliding between cameras
payload.decision: Within Q-113 and Q-120; no contract or server change. (1) State: the workspace keeps, for this DM view only, the live scene Follow my view was turned on for; another scene going live or the TV going idle (the live scene's id changing) turns it off, so every activation starts with it off, while a snapshot of the same live scene (a reconnection, a setup change) leaves it on. Lock TV camera turns it off and disables the toggle. Only the DM view's own controls turn it off: no `camera.player` event, its own echo or another DM browser's steering, does, and none moves the DM's camera. (2) The camera: `followRect` (`client/src/canvas/geometry.ts`) takes the DM view's whole visible area and widens it about its centre to the shape of the screen the TV frame follows (D-119), 16:9 while none has reported, a wider TV widening it and a narrower one raising it, never shrinking either side; it then keeps the camera within `CAMERA_BOUNDS` by one factor on both sides, so the shape holds, and its centre on the world as the contract requires. The canvas reports it whenever the DM's view or the TV's shape changes. (3) Sending: `camera.setPlayer` through a throttle (`client/src/dm/live/throttle.ts`, 100 ms), the first change at once, the latest of each interval at its end, so the camera a pan or zoom ends on is always sent; a camera equal to the one sent last is not sent. Turning it off by any control drops what waits before the control acts. A follow send never clears another failure notice; a refusal is shown like a refused TV camera. Nothing is sent while not connected, and it resumes on reconnection. (4) Paused (Q-120): only the live scene's panel sends; another scene's panel sends nothing and the live indicator says "Follow paused"; the live scene's panel, opened again, sends its view at once. (5) UI: the toggle among the TV camera controls, filled in the accent colour while on; the TV frame and its dimming are not drawn while on, the canvas's edge ringed in the accent colour instead, since the TV shows at least the whole view; the live indicator shows "TV follows you"; C toggles it on the live scene, listed in the shortcut bar, whose note then says the TV follows the view. (6) The player view glides to each new camera in 120 ms, eased out, the zoom changing evenly in proportion and the centre in a straight line, so a TV following the DM does not step ten times a second; a new world or screen size, the first camera and reduced motion take it at once.
payload.why: The server already holds everything Follow my view needs (`camera.setPlayer`, the screen registry, `camera.player` to both rooms), so keeping its state in the DM view adds no command, no stored state and nothing for the players' room to filter. The live scene's id is what changes on an activation or on going idle, and only then. Widening rather than fitting is what `04` §9 asks: the TV crops nothing the DM sees. Trailing sends guarantee the TV settles where the DM stopped; cancelling on a manual control keeps a waiting follow camera from undoing it. Hiding the frame avoids a frame drawn mostly off screen that could not be dragged anyway.
payload.alternatives: A follow state on the server, with its own command (rejected by the brief: no new command, and the server would have to know which DM browser's camera to follow); a debounce that sends only when a gesture ends (rejected: the TV would not move during a long pan); drawing the frame locked to the viewport's edges (rejected: the widened frame lies partly outside the canvas on a TV of another shape, so its edges would be off screen; the accent ring says the same); F or L as the shortcut (rejected: F is the fog brush, and L reads as Lock); no glide on the TV (rejected: 10 Hz steps are visible on a large screen; 120 ms keeps Send my view immediate).

payload.title: DMT-04: notes on their own REST routes, told to the DM room as notes.updated, 20,000 characters, saved as typed in the DM view, N for the scene's
payload.decision: Within Q-114 and D-181. Contract (`shared/src/notes.ts`): `notes` on Scene and Token, plain text, empty by default; `SceneTokenSchema.asset` gains its asset's `notes`, so the DM's token carries what is shown beside its own, while `PlayerTokenSchema`, built field by field, carries neither; `NOTES_MAX_LENGTH` 20,000 characters, counted by code point as JSON Schema counts, on notes bodies and on an asset's notes too, so nothing a token shows is unbounded. Routes: `PUT /api/scenes/:id/notes` and `PUT /api/tokens/:id/notes`, each the whole text, last write winning, on any scene, the live one included; they answer the Scene or the DM's token. On the live scene they send the DM room `notes.updated { scene_id, token_id or null, notes }`, taking its next version, and never a snapshot; the players room hears nothing and its version does not move. Notes are in no undo history: undo of a token's deletion puts it back with its notes, as with every other field. Storage: migration 0012 adds `scene.notes` and `token.notes`, `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` with a CHECK of length() at most 20,000; additive, rollback is the dated backup. Duplication copies the scene's notes and every token's notes, hit points and armour class (DMT-01's copy left the hit points out; fixed here, as `03` §7 has required since D-181). An asset's notes changed while one of its tokens is on the live scene reach the DM room as a snapshot (`refresh` already compares them), players nothing. DM view: no Save button; `NotesEditor` saves 500 ms after typing stops and on blur, saying "Saving…", "Saved" or "Not saved yet" quietly; a failed save keeps the text, says why and is sent again with the next change or on blur; a text over the limit is kept, not sent, with the limit and the count; text not yet stored when its field goes (popover closed, scene switched) is sent then and kept in memory until the server has it, the field opened again showing it; the browser asks before leaving while any is unsaved. A `notes.updated` (or a refreshed record) never replaces a field that is focused or holds unsaved text: "Changed in another window" says so, the DM's own save winning; once left with nothing unsaved the field shows the server's. The field's own save echoed by the live connection before its answer is not taken for another window's. Notes are only ever a textarea's value or a text node: no `innerHTML`. Placement: the scene's notes in a fourth right-hand tab, Notes, between Initiative and Library, for the scene open (live or not); N opens it with the cursor in the field (Shift+N stays Go live next; nothing else used N), on the shortcut bar. A token's notes at the end of its popover, four rows, long ones collapsed to three lines with Show more, its asset's under them read-only, headed "From {name} (library)"; the popover now scrolls within the canvas rather than run past it. Marks: a page badge on the left edge of a token with notes of its own or from its asset on the DM's map only (its first lines as the canvas's title on hover), the same mark on its "In this scene" row, a mark on the thumbnail of a scene with notes in the scene list, each with the first lines as its hover text; the turn's row of the initiative order has a notes button when its token has any, opening the popover centred with the cursor in the notes. A focus request (D's for hit points, the initiative's for notes) now belongs to the popover and the token it was made for, so a popover opened again later takes no focus of itself, which DMT-01's D did.
payload.why: Dedicated routes keep notes apart from setup, which on the live scene goes to both rooms as a snapshot, and from the token routes, which refuse the live scene: `04` §2 and §16 want notes editable at any time, and a route of their own needs no exception in either. A DM-room event rather than a DM snapshot keeps the DM's version counter and payloads small while typing. The limit bounds what every DM token event carries. Autosave with the text kept on every failure is required because notes are not undoable: until the server has the text, the field is its only copy.
payload.alternatives: `notes` in `PATCH /api/scenes/:id` and `PATCH /api/tokens/:id` (rejected: the first sends a snapshot of the live scene for every keystroke pause, the second refuses the live scene's tokens); a live command (rejected by D-181: notes are not undoable and never reach the TV); copying an asset's notes into each new token (rejected: `03` §10 shows the asset's beside the token's, read-only, and a later edit of the asset should show); a Save button (rejected by the brief); overwriting a focused field with another window's text (rejected: it would lose typing); Ctrl+Shift+N or Alt+N (rejected: browsers take Ctrl+Shift+N, and N was free); no limit on asset notes (rejected: every DM token event carries them).

payload.title: DMT-05: export and import as a zip of format 1, read by yauzl from its central directory, written by yazl as it streams, every refusal storing nothing
payload.decision: Within Q-115, Q-119 and D-181. Contract (`shared/src/archive.ts`): format 1 (`ARCHIVE_FORMAT_VERSION`), `manifest.json` (`format_version`, `app_version`, `exported_at`, `kind` campaign or assets, `counts` of campaigns, sessions, scenes, tokens, encounters, assets and images, and the image hashes), `data/<name>.json` (campaign, sessions, scenes, tokens, encounters, assets, images for a campaign; assets and images for library assets) and `images/<sha256>.<png|jpg|webp>`, nothing else (`ARCHIVE_ENTRY_PATTERN`); every record is the DM's REST record checked strictly by the shared schemas, a scene adding its `token_numbers` and `fog`, a token its `shown`, an asset its tags, an image no variants; `migrateFormat` is the place a later format upgrades an older archive, a no-op for 1. Routes (`02` §5's `/api/export` and `/api/import`): `GET /api/export/campaigns/:id`, `GET /api/export/assets` (repeated `id`, or the whole library), `POST /api/import` (the zip as the body, any Content-Type), `GET /api/import/progress` (the running import's stage: receiving, reading, images with a count, saving); all behind the DM session and the Origin check. Settings: migration 0013 adds `import_limit_bytes`, 2 GiB, bounded 1 MiB to 64 GiB, in `PATCH /api/settings`, read at each import. Errors: `import_busy` (409), `import_too_large` (413), `import_newer_format` (422, with `format_version` in the envelope), `import_unsafe_entry`, `import_invalid` and `import_image_refused` (422), each with the archive entry and an English reason in `details`. Export: one read transaction, then yazl streams the zip as it is sent (images stored, JSON deflated); the file name is `<campaign>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.zip` made safe for Windows, or `library-<YYYY-MM-DD>.zip`. Import: the body streamed to a file in its own folder under `images/.incoming` (removed at the end, and at every start), refused as soon as it passes the limit, without destroying the request so the browser reads the 413; yauzl opens the file by its central directory with its own size checks off (`decodeStrings` and `validateEntrySizes` false) because the server makes them: every name from its raw bytes (printable ASCII, no absolute path, drive letter, backslash, `.` or `..` segment, only the layout), no duplicate, no link or special file (Unix mode or the Windows reparse attribute), no encryption, stored or deflated only, at most 100,000 entries, the declared total within the limit; then each entry's real bytes are counted as they inflate and the read stops at the first chunk past what its headers declared, past its cap (16 MiB for the manifest, 64 MiB a data file, the upload limit an image) or past the limit in total, and its size and CRC-32 are checked at its end. Order: the manifest's format version first, then the layout of its kind, the data against the schemas, the references (counts and image lists agree; every id once; sessions of the campaign, scenes of its sessions, tokens of its scenes, one encounter per scene and each entry a token of that scene; a token's asset, a scene's map and an asset's image in the archive or on the server; tags normalised), then each image received by the upload's own `receive` and checked by its `processUpload` (type from content, the upload limit, a full decode), its sha256 against its name, its type against its extension and record; one the server holds is reused without decoding (same bytes). Storing is one synchronous step: one SQLite transaction checks the references again against the server at that moment, reuses an existing asset as it is, inserts an asset it lacks under its own id, gives the campaign, sessions, scenes, tokens, encounter and entries new ids through one map per entity applied to every reference, the name taking " (2)", " (3)"… when taken, `character_id` null; the staged images are renamed into the images folder last, inside the transaction's function, and any failure removes the folders moved and rolls back. One import at a time, the second refused before its body is read; an import changes no live state and is allowed while a scene is live. DM view: Export on each campaign's row of the tree (a download link) and one Import beside New campaign; in the library, Import and a Select mode with a check box per asset, Export selected (n) and Export all; the Import dialog with the upload's progress, then the server's stage ("Checking images… 3 of 26"), the summary ("Imported Curse of the Fallen: 3 sessions, 12 scenes, 45 tokens · 4 new assets, 8 reused · 20 images reused, 6 new") or the reason with "Nothing was changed." and the server's detail; Settings' import limit in MB beside the upload limit, one hint for both, so the dialog still fits 620 px (G-041). Dependencies: yauzl 3.4 and yazl 3.3 (MIT, pure JavaScript, bundled into the package by esbuild). The package's bundle now defines `__EMBERGLASS_VERSION__`, read by `server/src/version.ts` for `app_version`.
payload.why: `07` §9 asks for refusals that store nothing and an archive no larger than the limit once unpacked; counting the bytes the server inflates, rather than trusting any header, is what makes the limit hold against a zip that lies, and a central-directory reader over a file on disk is what lets an archive of gigabytes be read without memory. Checking the images with the upload's own functions keeps `05` §6 one rule. Producing the display version and thumbnail in the staging folder, before the transaction, rather than after the commit as the brief for this package put it, is the stricter reading of 'stores nothing': a variant that fails to be made refuses the import instead of leaving an image row without its files; renaming the staged folders inside the transaction's function, last, does the same for a rename that fails, and no other request can run in between. One map per entity keeps a hostile archive that reuses one uuid across kinds from crossing references.
payload.alternatives: Generating variants after the commit (the brief's order; rejected for the reason above); reading the archive in memory or with a streaming reader of local headers (rejected: local headers are not authoritative and can disagree with the central directory, and memory is unbounded); trusting yauzl's own size check alone (kept off so the server's counter is what refuses, testably; its result would be the same refusal earlier for a lying header); refusing a campaign whose name exists (rejected: the brief and Q-115 ask for a copy, renamed); renumbering session and scene orders on import (rejected: a copy should read back unchanged; duplicate orders are refused); a POST export with the ids in a body (rejected: a browser download of a POST cannot stream to disk; repeated `id` in the query string, as the asset list's `tag`, bounded to 1,000); an import job polled by id (rejected: one import at a time makes a single progress route enough).

payload.title: A collapsible scene sidebar
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-05 (UI/UX refinements), asked in the planning session of that day.
payload.question: How should the DM view's left sidebar (the session's scenes and Next up) make room for the map?
options: A) It collapses to a strip at the left edge by default; hovering near that edge opens it over the map and moving away closes it; a toggle opens it on click and a pin docks it in its column, remembered per browser → effect on ux: the map gains the sidebar's width, the scenes stay a hover away.
B) Both side panels collapse the same way → effect on ux: more map, but the Library tab, the source of a drag to the map, hides too.
C) The same mechanics, docked by default → effect on ux: nothing changes until the DM unpins it.
payload.recommendation: A, because the scene list is consulted between scenes while the right panel is in use all the time.

payload.title: Selecting several tokens at once
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-05 (UI/UX refinements), asked in the planning session of that day.
payload.question: Can the DM select several tokens and act on them together, and with what?
options: A) Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and a click add or remove a token from the selection, on the map and in the token list; a drag of any selected token moves them all, keeping their offsets, the arrow keys nudge them all; a bar offers Hide or Reveal, a condition toggled on all, one amount of damage or healing on each, and Delete with one confirmation → effect on ux: groups of monsters handled in one gesture.
B) Only moving together → effect on ux: the other actions stay one token at a time.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner asked.

payload.title: One undo step for an action on a group of tokens
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-05 (UI/UX refinements), asked in the planning session of that day.
payload.question: On the live scene, how does undo treat an action on several selected tokens?
options: A) One batched command, `token.batch`, carrying the move, visibility, marker, hit-point and delete commands of the group, applied all or nothing in one transaction and undone and redone as one step; each effect projected to the players room as its single command's → effect on data: one new live command and a compound inverse; the hidden-information suite covers it.
B) One command per token → effect on data: no contract change, but undoing a group of five takes five Ctrl+Z.
payload.recommendation: A, because a group action is one decision of the DM and the history is bounded to 100 steps.

payload.title: Dragging a token from the library onto the map
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-05 (UI/UX refinements), asked in the planning session of that day.
payload.question: Can the DM add a token by dragging an asset from the Library tab onto the map, and what becomes of the picker?
options: A) Yes, beside the picker: a library asset dragged onto the map is placed where it is dropped, snapped as a placed token is, Alt for no snapping; the picker stays, keyboard-operable, its rows laid out with the thumbnail, the name and the Choose button on one line → effect on ux: the drag `01` §6 put off arrives, and the keyboard flow is kept.
B) No, the picker alone → effect on ux: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner asked, keeping the picker as the keyboard alternative.

payload.title: The player view on phones, tablets and large screens
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-05 (UI/UX refinements), asked in the planning session of that day.
payload.question: Can the read-only player view be opened on phones and tablets, and what may it offer there?
options: A) The player view lays out for any screen from a phone to a large desktop; on a touch device without hover it offers a fullscreen button where the browser supports it and pinch and drag to zoom and pan its own view, with a button and a double tap returning to the DM's camera; it still sends no command, a handheld reports no viewport so the TV frame keeps the TV's shape, and the TV keeps no controls → effect on scope: phones become screens of the table, still read-only, still filtered on the server; the DM's camera is a handheld's starting view, not its limit.
B) TV and projector only, as Q-054 and `01` §4 say → effect on scope: no change.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner asked; nothing hidden reaches a handheld, which receives exactly what the TV does.

payload.title: UI/UX refinements (Phase 8): a collapsible scene sidebar, multi-select with token.batch, drag from the library, a compact campaigns menu and a responsive player view on handhelds
payload.decision: The owner's decisions of 2026-10-05, recorded as cards Q-121 to Q-125, each answered A. (1) Q-121: the DM view's left sidebar collapses to an edge strip by default, opens over the map on hover or by its toggle, closes when the pointer leaves, and a pin docks it in its column, remembered per browser. (2) Q-122: Ctrl or Cmd and a click add a token to the selection or remove it, on the map and in the token list; a drag of a selected token moves the group, the arrow keys nudge it, and a group bar offers Hide or Reveal, a condition toggled on all, one damage or healing amount on each, and Delete with one confirmation. (3) Q-123: on the live scene a group action is one command, token.batch, of 1 to 50 token.move, token.setVisibility, token.setMarkers, token.applyHp and token.delete commands, applied all or nothing in one transaction and undone and redone as one step; each effect is projected to the players room exactly as its single command's is, nothing naming the batch or its size; on a prepared scene the group's REST writes are sent one per token. (4) Q-124: a library asset dragged onto the map is placed where it is dropped, snapped as a placed token, Alt for none; the picker stays as the keyboard path, its rows on one line. (5) Q-125: the player view lays out for phones, tablets and large desktops; on a touch device without hover (pointer coarse, hover none) it shows a fullscreen button where the browser supports element fullscreen and takes pinch and drag to zoom and pan its own view, reset by a button shown while zoomed, by a double tap and by every activation; a handheld sends no command and reports no viewport, so the TV frame keeps the TV's shape (D-119); the TV and any fine-pointer screen keep no controls (Q-054). On a handheld the DM's camera is the starting view, not a limit: zooming out shows what that screen already holds, which the server filtered exactly as for the TV.
payload.why: The owner asked for these changes on 2026-10-05 and approved overriding the decisions they touch: Q-054 and D-031 (no controls on the player view), Q-029 (touch), `01` §2 and §4 (no player devices; a mobile UI in Phase 2), `01` §6 and `05` §5 (drag from the sidebar later; the picker flow only) and `04` §2 (the closed list of live token commands). Hidden information is unaffected: a handheld is a players-room socket like the TV, receives the same filtered snapshots, events and display images, and sends nothing.
payload.alternatives: Both side panels collapsing (rejected: the Library tab is the source of the drag to the map); one command per token on a group (rejected: a group of five takes five undo steps out of a history of 100); TV-only player view (rejected by the owner); a phone driving the TV frame's shape (rejected: a phone connected before the TV would set it, so handhelds report no viewport); a handheld zoom bounded by the DM's camera (rejected: the camera is framing, not hidden information, and a phone read at arm's length needs to look around).

payload.title: Q-121 to Q-125 written into the specs: Phase 8, the UI/UX refinements, with the defaults the owner's answers leave open
