payload.decision: Writes D-188 into the specs by `make unlock` of `01`, `04`, `05`, `08`, `10`, `11`, `12`, `13` and `14`. `01` §2: the player screen may be a phone or tablet, read-only, no player device; §4: the mobile UI of Phase 2 excludes it; §6: the drag arrives in Phase 8; new §11 lists Phase 8. `04` §2: `token.batch` in the command table and the closed list, all or nothing, not nesting, projected as its commands one by one; §8: a batch is one undo step. `05` §5: the drag from the library beside the picker. `08` §1 and §3: the collapsible sidebar and the multi-select; §7: the player view on phones, tablets and large screens, touch on a coarse pointer without hover; §9: the fullscreen and reset buttons there only; new §14: the DM view's and the handheld player view's refinements. `10` §3: the hidden-information script gains a batch and its undo; §4: the player view accepted on an emulated phone and tablet and once by hand on real devices. `11`, `12` §3 and §5 and `14` §3 follow. `13` §2 and new §13: Phase 8, UXR-01 to UXR-05, with derived characteristics. AGENTS.md's scope and play red lines name Phase 8 and `token.batch`. Defaults the owner's answers leave open, tagged [D-189] or carried by the cards' option text, each open to the owner: the campaigns menu's icons and tooltips (the owner's brief, not a card); a batch holds 1 to 50 commands; a handheld is a screen whose primary pointer is coarse and cannot hover; its zoom runs from the whole map to eight times the DM's camera; it reports no viewport; the real-device run is owed by hand.
payload.why: The amendment regime (D-002) requires the owner's answers in the specs before code, and the derived characteristics of each package are checked by `make check-docs`.
payload.alternatives: Leaving the refinements as implementation decisions only (rejected: they cross locked bullets of `12` and red lines of AGENTS.md, which need the spec text to move with them).

payload.title: UXR-01: the scene sidebar's dock, opened by hover or by a click, and the end-to-end contexts starting docked
payload.decision: Within Q-121. `client/src/dm/SidebarDock.tsx` wraps the scene list and Next up. Collapsed (the default), a 16 px strip (`--sidebar-strip`) holds the toggle (`Show scenes` / `Hide scenes`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`); the sidebar is absolutely placed over the map, slid out and made `inert` while closed. Two ways open it: hover (pointer enter on the strip or the sidebar; a touch pointer ignored), closed 250 ms after the pointer leaves (`SIDEBAR_CLOSE_MS`) unless a drag that started in it, a dialog of its own or a keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) holds it; and a click on the toggle, which keeps it open until the toggle, Escape or a press outside it. Keyboard focus moving into it opens it as hover does. The pin (`Keep scenes open` / `Let scenes collapse`, `aria-pressed`) docks it in its 256 px column, as before Phase 8, remembered in localStorage under `emberglass.sidebar` (every access in try/catch; refused storage starts collapsed); unpinning moves the focus to the toggle. The Playwright config's `storageState` starts every context with the sidebar docked, so the specs written before Phase 8 reach the scene list in its column as a DM who pinned it does; `redesign.spec.ts` covers the collapsed default in a context without it, and the keyboard walk re-docks it before every reopening since it operates the pin.
payload.why: A click-opened sidebar that closed as the pointer left would fight a DM who clicked to use it; hover-open needs the grace period so that a diagonal move to the list does not close it. Docking the end-to-end contexts keeps sixty-odd specs about other features from each learning to open the sidebar.
payload.alternatives: Every spec opening the sidebar through a helper (rejected: dozens of direct uses of the scene list, and no feature of theirs is the sidebar); hover alone without the click (rejected: the owner asked for a button too); resizing the map when it opens (rejected by Q-121).

payload.title: UXR-03: a library asset dragged onto the map, by HTML5 drag and drop under its own type, the picker's rows on one line
payload.decision: Within Q-124. A library row is `draggable` outside the export selection mode; its drag carries the asset's identifier under `application/x-emberglass-asset` (`client/src/dm/library/assetDrag.ts`), `effectAllowed` copy, the thumbnail as the drag image, and the dragged asset is kept in that module because a drop target reads the drag's data only on the drop. `MapCanvas` takes an `assetDrop` prop (DM mode, not while calibrating): `dragover` accepts only that type, computes the drop point from the pointer through the camera with the same `placeAt` a click uses (centred, snapped, Alt for none, kept on the map) and draws the footprint as `drop-target`, exposed to the end-to-end tests as `data-dropping`; `drop` hands the grid point to `ScenePanel`, whose `placeToken` places it on a prepared scene over REST or on the live one by `token.add`, selecting it with its popover, exactly as a click after the picker does. Any other drag (files, text) is not taken. The picker's rows (`.eg-picker__item`) lay out the thumbnail, the name and Choose on one line, the whole row choosing; the library's own Edit and Delete became icon buttons at the row's end, their names unchanged.
payload.why: Reusing `placeAt` and `placeToken` keeps one placement rule for click, Enter and drop; a module-level holder is the only way to know the asset's size during `dragover`.
payload.alternatives: Dragging from the picker dialog (rejected: a modal dialog makes the map behind it inert); reading the size from a second drag type carrying it (rejected: types are lower-cased strings, a footprint needs the asset, and the holder already has it).

payload.title: UXR-02: token.batch, all or nothing in one transaction with a compound inverse, and the DM view's selection of several tokens
payload.decision: Within Q-122 and Q-123. Contract (`shared/src/live.ts`): `token.batch` in `COMMAND_TYPES`, payload `{ commands }`, 1 to `MAX_BATCH_COMMANDS` (50) entries, each `{ type, payload }` of `BATCH_COMMAND_TYPES` (`token.move`, `token.setVisibility`, `token.setMarkers`, `token.applyHp`, `token.delete`) with that command's own strict payload schema, as a union, so a nested batch, `token.add`, `token.setStats` or an extra field is refused by validation. The command validator now checks that every object nested in a payload is a plain JSON object, so no binary attachment hides inside a batch. Server (`server/src/domain/live.ts`): `applyBatch` runs each entry through `applyLiveCommand` inside one outer better-sqlite3 transaction, the inner ones nesting as savepoints; the first refusal is thrown out of it, rolling the whole batch back, and is the batch's answer; the effects are concatenated in order and published as single commands' are, so each room's projection is unchanged and nothing names the batch or its size. Undo (`server/src/domain/undo.ts`): the compound inverse `{ type: 'batch', inverses }` of the entries that changed something; `replay` applies it last first in one transaction, all or nothing, and answers the compound of its parts' own inverses, so undo, redo and undo again each take one step; a batch that changed nothing records none. Client: `ScenePanel` keeps `selection`, the primary last; Ctrl or Cmd and a press on the map (`TokenLayer`, `togglesSelection`) or a click on a row (`TokenList`) toggles; a press on a member keeps the group, a click without a drag selects it alone; a drag of a member moves the others with it (`onDragMove`) and drops them by the primary's snapped offset (no clamp, as a single drag); the arrow keys nudge each; Escape clears. With two or more, no popover: `GroupBar` floats over the top of the map (not above it, so its appearance moves nothing under the pointer) with Hide or Reveal (H), a condition menu of all eighteen, a damage or healing amount (a set number refused for a group), Delete asked once (`DeleteGroupDialog`) and Clear. `dm/tokens/group.ts` builds each action's commands, only for tokens it changes. On the live scene one `token.batch`, shown at once through `pending`; in preparation the same changes over REST one token at a time. There is no per-command rate limit to count a batch in.
payload.why: Running every entry through the single-command path keeps one rule per command and one projection; the compound inverse replayed in reverse is the only order in which a group of moves, hides and deletions takes itself back exactly.
payload.alternatives: A dedicated `token.moveMany` (rejected: the group bar needs visibility, markers, hit points and deletion too); one command per token (rejected by the owner, Q-123); clamping each member of a dropped group to the map (not done: a single drag does not clamp either, and the coordinate bounds are far beyond any map); the group bar above the map (rejected: appearing on the second Ctrl-click it moved the map under the pointer, so the release fell on empty map and cleared the selection).

payload.title: UXR-05: the player view on handhelds, a touch view composed over the DM's camera, fullscreen where the browser can, no viewport report
payload.decision: Within Q-125. A handheld is `(pointer: coarse) and (hover: none)` (`client/src/player/useHandheld.ts`); everything below applies to it alone, and a TV or desktop renders as before, with nothing that takes focus. The touch view (`client/src/player/touchView.ts`) is a zoom and a screen-pixel offset composed over the camera the DM steers (`compose`), bounded so the screen's centre stays over the map and the zoom stays between the whole map (the fitted scale over the DM camera's, at most 1) and 8 (`bounded`); `MapCanvas` takes it as the player-mode `touch` prop and its glides keep running under it. Gestures (`useTouchGestures`) read pointer events on the canvas element, `touch-action: none`: one pointer pans, two pinch around their midpoint and pan with it, two taps within 300 ms and 30 px reset; pointer capture is best-effort. `PlayerView` keeps the view per scene identity (name and map), so another scene going live starts at the DM's camera; the same scene made live again keeps it (players are told no scene id, and a setup edit's fresh snapshot must not reset a look-around). Buttons bottom right (48 px, `Full screen` / `Leave full screen` with `aria-pressed`, and `Back to the table view` while zoomed) fade 3 s after the last touch and take no taps while faded; fullscreen is `requestFullscreen` on `main`, or the webkit-prefixed one, shown only when the document says it can, so not on an iPhone. `usePlayerLive` skips `reportViewport` on a handheld, so the TV frame's shape is the TV's (D-119). Labels on a handheld scale by the shorter side, at least the DM view's own size (`handheldLabelScaleFor`). CSS: safe-area insets for the plate and strip (`viewport-fit=cover`), below 700 px the strip names only the current token, with smaller portraits, and on a handheld it scrolls sideways with room for its NOW and NEXT tags.
payload.why: Composing over the steered camera keeps the DM's control (a pan or Follow my view still moves the handheld) while the screen looks around; keying by scene identity is the only activation signal a player has.
payload.alternatives: An independent camera on the handheld (rejected: it would stop following the DM); resetting on every snapshot (rejected: a setup edit or a reconnect would throw the zoom away); letting a handheld report its size (rejected: a phone connected first would set the TV frame's shape).

payload.title: UXR-01 redesigned after the owner's review: a 56 px rail with the scenes at a glance, the sidebar a floating card, the pin in its header; More… opens inside the popover
payload.decision: Within Q-121 and D-190, after the owner found the edge strip and the floating pin poor. Collapsed, the sidebar is a 56 px rail (`--sidebar-rail`): a 36 px toggle, then the session's scenes as 36 px thumbnails, the one shown ringed in the accent, the live one with a live-coloured dot; the thumbnails are an overview only (`aria-hidden`), since hovering the rail opens the sidebar where scenes are chosen. Open, the sidebar is a card inset 8 px over the rail and the map, rounded and shadowed, fading and sliding in. The pin moved from a bar above the title into the scene list's header beside New scene (`SceneList` `actions`, the dock passing it through a render prop), pressed in the accent while docked. Behaviour, keys, the close delay and the remembered pin are D-190's. Separately, the popover's More… list was an absolutely placed 200 px box beside the chip: inside the popover, which scrolls, it overflowed sideways, adding both scrollbars and clipping the list. It now opens as a full-width row under the chips (the wrapper `display: contents`, the box `flex: 1 0 100%`), its conditions in two columns, the popover hiding sideways overflow and scrolling the list into view; `markers.spec.ts` asserts the popover never scrolls sideways.
payload.why: The owner's review of 2026-10-05: the sidebar works but looks rough, and More… broke the popover.
payload.alternatives: A rail whose thumbnails select a scene (rejected: hover opens the sidebar before a thumbnail can be clicked); the More… list drawn outside the popover in the body (rejected: it would float away from the popover when the popover scrolls).

payload.title: Clicking a token again, and previewing a token on hover
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-06 (more UI/UX refinements), asked in the session of that day.
payload.question: How should a click on a token whose popover is already open behave, and can the DM look a token up without opening its popover?
options: A) A second click on the token whose popover is open closes it, the token staying selected; and the mouse resting on a token for about half a second shows a read-only preview beside it (name, visibility, hit points, armour class, conditions, the whole of its notes), which a pointer passing over tokens while preparing never triggers, and which leaving, pressing, zooming or another tool hides at once → effect on ux: the popover toggles like a switch and the essentials are a glance away.
B) Only the toggle → effect on ux: looking a token up still opens its popover.
C) The preview at once on hover, with no delay → effect on ux: cards flash up over the map whenever the pointer crosses a token.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner asked; a delay of about half a second with a resting pointer: the rest test already keeps a sweeping pointer from triggering it, and the owner found a second too slow.

payload.title: UXR-06: a second click on a token closes its popover, and a resting mouse previews the token, read-only
payload.decision: The owner's decision of 2026-10-06, recorded as card Q-126, answered A. (1) A click on the token whose popover is open closes the popover; the token stays selected, as after a drag (D-156). (2) In the DM view, the mouse resting on a token, while tokens can be selected, shows beside it a read-only preview: its label, whether players can see it, its hit points and armour class, its conditions and the whole of its notes, or of its asset's when it has none. A pointer passing over a token, a touch, a held button and the token whose popover is open show none; leaving the token, pressing it, zooming or another tool hide it at once. The preview takes neither the pointer nor the focus and is never drawn on the player view.
payload.why: The owner asked for both on 2026-10-06. The toggle extends Q-102's click without changing a drag or a pan; the preview is read from the DM's own tokens, which already carry everything it shows, so nothing new reaches either room and hidden information is unaffected.
payload.alternatives: Only the toggle (rejected by the owner); a preview at once on hover (rejected: cards would flash over the map while the DM prepares); a delay of one or two seconds (rejected: the owner found a second too slow; the rest test already keeps a sweeping pointer from triggering a shorter one).

payload.title: Q-126 written into the specs: UXR-06, the token's popover closed by a second click and its preview on hover
payload.decision: Writes D-195 into the specs by `make unlock` of `01`, `08`, `11` and `13`. `01` §11: a new bullet for the toggle and the preview. `08` §11: the Q-102 bullet gains the second click closing the popover; §14: a new bullet for the preview, its contents and when it shows and hides. `11`: the UI/UX refinements row names them and Q-126. `13` §13: the goal names looking a token up, and UXR-06 with its exit criteria and derived characteristics; `13` §2 names Q-126. AGENTS.md's scope red line names them and Q-126. Default the owner's answer leaves open, tagged by the card's option text and open to the owner: about half a second of rest.
payload.why: The amendment regime (D-002) requires the owner's answer in the specs before the package is done, and its derived characteristics are checked by `make check-docs`.
payload.alternatives: Leaving it an implementation decision (rejected: AGENTS.md's scope red line lists the UI/UX refinements one by one, owner-approved).

payload.title: UXR-06: the preview after 500 ms of a mouse resting within 6 px, reported by the token layer, drawn by the scene panel, never an .eg-popover
payload.decision: Within Q-126 and D-195; no contract or server change. (1) Toggle: the scene panel's `onOpenPopover` closes the popover when it is open on the token clicked and no group is selected; the token layer is unchanged, so a press that becomes a drag, another token's press, a pan, Escape and a click on empty map behave as D-156 has them. (2) Hover intent (`client/src/canvas/hoverIntent.ts`): `PREVIEW_DELAY_MS` 500 and `REST_TOLERANCE_PX` 6; each move farther than 6 px from where the wait began starts it again, so a sweeping pointer never reaches it; a preview shown stays while the mouse moves over its own token; moving onto another token hides it at once and waits for that one. (3) The token layer feeds it from `pointerenter` and `pointermove` only for `pointerType` mouse with no button held, and cancels it on `pointerleave`, `pointerdown`, `wheel`, a move with a button held, its controls going (a tool, a pan by Space, placing, calibrating) and unmounting. (4) The map canvas keeps the previewed id while tokens can be selected and places the preview with the popover's own placement (`placement`, exported from `TokenPopover.tsx`), 280 px wide, moved up once measured so that it stays on the canvas, a note taller than the canvas fading out at its bottom. (5) The popover's hit-point editor lays its three fields in columns of minmax(0, 1fr), each input filling its column, so no engine widens a column to the input's default size and the popover never scrolls sideways. (6) The scene panel renders `TokenPreview`, none for the token whose popover is open and none while an asset is being placed: role tooltip, `pointer-events: none`, no focusable element; the label, the visibility line, hit points as current / max with temporary ones and the bar, the armour class on a shield, a dash for either missing, the conditions as small labelled pills with their icons and Exhaustion's level, the whole of the token's notes, else its asset's under "From {name} (library)", and "Click the token to edit it."; a 120 ms fade, none under reduced motion. Its root class is `eg-preview`, never `eg-popover`, so every test and end-to-end locator of the popover keeps meaning the popover. The note badge's title (D-186) is kept.
payload.why: Half a second is quick enough that the owner, who found 1,000 ms too slow, does not wait for it, and the rest test keeps preparation undisturbed: a pointer moving or dragging across a crowded map does not stay within 6 px on one token for 500 ms by accident. Reading only the DM's own `SceneToken` keeps the preview out of the players' room by construction. A separate root class avoids two `.eg-popover` elements on the page.
payload.alternatives: 1,000 ms (the first implementation; the owner found it too slow) and two seconds (the owner's first figure); a timer that only starts on `pointerenter` (rejected: a pointer crossing a large token slowly would trigger it); the preview inside the popover component (rejected: the popover is editable and takes the pointer); a Konva-drawn card (rejected: text layout, line clamping and theming are the DOM's).

payload.title: UXR-07: while a row is dragged the others make room for it, sliding, so its slot shows where it will land
payload.decision: Within Q-127 and D-199 (`08` §12); no contract or server change, `encounter.reorder` sent once, on the drop. (1) While a row is dragged, the order shown is recomputed on each `dragover` of another row (`dragOrder`, `client/src/dm/initiative/reorder.ts`): the dragged row takes that row's place once the pointer has crossed its middle in the direction of travel, so a row sliding away under the pointer never swaps back; several rows at once when the pointer jumps. (2) Every row that changes place slides from where it was drawn to its new place in 160 ms, eased out (`useSlidingRows`, the Web Animations API over layout positions), none under reduced motion; numbers typed and other DM windows' reorders slide too. (3) The dragged row's slot is dimmed with a dashed focus-coloured outline, applied after the browser takes the drag image; the old insertion line is gone. (4) A drop anywhere in the list, its own slot included, sends the order shown, which stays shown until the encounter's order changes or the command is refused; a drag ending outside the list, or Escape, puts the order back and sends nothing. (5) Now and Next follow their entries, not their indices, while the preview moves rows; Move up and Move down act on the stored order.
payload.why: The owner asked for the rows to move as the DM drags, so the place a row will take is plain before it is dropped. Crossing the middle in the direction of travel is the usual sortable-list rule and is what keeps the preview from oscillating while rows slide.
payload.alternatives: An insertion line only (the previous behaviour; rejected by the owner); a drag library such as dnd-kit (rejected: a dependency for one list, and the native drag already passes the keyboard and end-to-end tests); sending a reorder on every crossing (rejected: one undo step and one TV update per drop).

payload.title: The initiative order dragged with the rows making room, numbers by the mouse wheel, and a TV strip of the turn and the next
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-06 (more UI/UX refinements), asked in the session of that day.
payload.question: How should the initiative tracker take a drag and a number in the DM view, and how much of the order should the TV's strip show?
options: A) While a row is dragged the other rows slide aside, so its slot shows where it will land before the drop; an initiative number can also be stepped by the mouse wheel over its field, sent when the wheel rests; the TV's strip shows only two cards, the turn and the next, replaced on every turn → effect on ux: a reorder is visible before it happens, numbers are set without typing, and the TV names who acts and who is up without listing the whole order.
B) The DM-view changes only, the TV's strip unchanged → effect on ux: the TV keeps listing every visible entry.
C) The TV's strip shows the turn alone → effect on ux: the next player does not see they are up.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner asked; the players' projection unchanged, so the strip shows less without the server sending more or less.

payload.title: UXR-07: the initiative order reflows while a row is dragged, numbers are stepped by the mouse wheel, and the TV's strip names only the turn and the next
payload.decision: The owner's decision of 2026-10-06, recorded as card Q-127, answered A. (1) While the DM drags a row of the initiative order, the other rows make room for it, sliding, so its slot shows where it will land; one reorder on the drop, none if it ends outside the list. (2) An initiative number may be stepped by the mouse wheel over its field, up raising it, an empty field starting at 10, sent once the wheel rests. (3) The TV's initiative strip shows two cards only, the entry whose turn it is and the next one, replaced on every turn; a turn players cannot see shows the next card alone.
payload.why: The owner asked for these on 2026-10-06. They override the strip of `08` §12 (a card for every visible entry, Q-111). Hidden information is unaffected: the players' projection of `04` §4 is unchanged and the strip shows a subset of it.
payload.alternatives: The DM-view changes only (rejected by the owner); the turn alone on the TV (rejected: the next player should see they are up); narrowing the players' projection to two entries (rejected: a change to the contract and the hidden-information suite for no gain, the projection already carrying only what players see).

payload.title: Q-127 written into the specs: UXR-07, the initiative refinements
payload.decision: Writes D-199 into the specs by `make unlock` of `01`, `08`, `11` and `13`. `01` §11: a bullet for the reflowing drag, the wheel and the two-card strip. `08` §12: the number field stepped by the mouse wheel, an empty one starting at 10; the player view's strip two cards only, the turn and the next, replaced on every turn. `11`: the UI/UX refinements row names them and Q-127. `13` §2 names Q-127; §13's goal names them, and UXR-07 with its exit criteria and derived characteristics (it touches a red line through `04` §4, so prompt 2 runs). AGENTS.md's scope red line names them and Q-127.
payload.why: The amendment regime (D-002) requires the owner's answer in the specs, and the package's derived characteristics are checked by `make check-docs`.
payload.alternatives: Folding them into UXR-06 (rejected: a separate concern, the initiative tracker, with its own red-line dimension).

payload.title: UXR-07: the wheel steps one per notch or 50 px, sent after 600 ms of rest or on leaving; the strip renders the projection's current and next
payload.decision: Within Q-127 and D-199; no contract or server change. (1) Wheel (`client/src/dm/initiative/wheel.ts`): a non-passive wheel listener on the number field, so the panel does not scroll under it; up adds one, down takes one, within -99 to 999; a line- or page-mode event is one step, a pixel-mode one (trackpads) one step per 50 px accumulated; an empty field starts at 10; each step shows at once and the number is sent once, 600 ms after the last step, or at once when the pointer leaves the field or it loses focus, so the row is not sorted away from under the pointer while the wheel turns; Ctrl and the wheel is left to the browser's zoom; the field's hover text says it can be scrolled. (2) Strip (`client/src/player/InitiativeStrip.tsx`): the cards are the entries at the projection's `current` and `next`, in that order, `current` null showing the next alone and `next` equal to `current` one card; keyed by round, turn and entry, so each turn's cards fade in (300 ms, none under reduced motion). The players' projection still carries every entry players see.
payload.why: Sending on rest rather than on each notch keeps one command, one undo step and one sort per adjustment. Rendering a subset leaves the hidden-information suite and the contract untouched.
payload.alternatives: Sending each notch (rejected: a row jumping on every notch, and many undo steps); the wheel only while the field has focus (rejected: a click before each adjustment; the field is small, so a page scroll rarely crosses it); a projection narrowed to two entries (rejected in D-199).

payload.title: Map notes: the DM's notes pinned at a point of the map
payload.source: The owner's brief of 2026-10-06 (map notes), asked in the session of that day.
payload.question: Can the DM place notes on a scene's map, and how do they behave?
options: A) Yes, on any scene, the live one included, DM-only: Add note (O) places one by a click; each is only a small icon of a constant size on the DM's map; a click opens its popover to read and edit it and a second click closes it; the mouse resting on it previews the whole text; a drag moves it, snapped to a square's centre; Delete in the popover, asked first; exported and imported with their campaign (archive format 2) → effect on scope: a new stored entity, routes, a DM-only event and an archive data file, filtered from players like every note.
B) Prep only → effect on scope: the same, but placed, moved and deleted only on scenes that are not live.
C) No map notes → effect on scope: none; scene and token notes only.
payload.recommendation: A, as the owner chose; the icon alone on the map, nothing beside it, as the owner asked.

payload.title: UXR-08: map notes, the DM's notes pinned on the map, on any scene, previewed on hover, exported with their campaign
payload.decision: The owner's decision of 2026-10-06, recorded as card Q-128, answered A. (1) A scene may carry map notes, each a plain-text note at a point of its map in grid units, the DM's only, deleted with the scene and copied when it is duplicated. (2) They are placed, edited, moved and deleted over REST on any scene, the live one included, and are not undoable; on the live scene each change reaches the dm room as `mapNotes.updated`, the scene's whole list, and the players room never. (3) In the DM view each is only a small icon of a constant size; Add note (O) places one by a click on the map; a click on its icon opens its popover (read and edit, Delete asked first) and a second click closes it; the mouse resting on it previews the whole text; a drag moves it. (4) A campaign's export carries them in data/mapnotes.json, archive format 2; a format-1 archive still imports, with none.
payload.why: The owner asked for map notes on 2026-10-06 and chose these answers. They add a stored entity (`03` §1, which listed exactly nine), a live event and an archive format, and touch the scope red line of AGENTS.md and the hidden-information rule, so an ADR. Hidden information: map notes are DM-only by construction, never read by the players' snapshot or sent to their room, and the hidden-information suite covers them.
payload.alternatives: Prep only (rejected by the owner); a title or label drawn beside the icon (rejected by the owner: the map gets crowded); map notes as fields of the scene's notes (rejected: no position); left out of exports (rejected by the owner).

payload.title: Q-128 written into the specs: UXR-08, map notes
payload.decision: Writes D-202 into the specs by `make unlock` of `01`, `02`, `03`, `04`, `08`, `09`, `10`, `11` and `13`. `01` §11: map notes among the refinements. `02` §5: their routes under the scene's. `03` §1: ten entities, MapNote (`scene_id`, `x`, `y`, `notes`); §2 its relationship; §7 deleted and copied with its scene; §10 DM-only. `04` §2: changed over REST at any time; §3: `mapNotes.updated`, players never; §4: never projected, a change moving no players' version; §16: their rule. `08` §14: Add note (O), the icon, the click toggle, the preview, the drag, Delete, an empty note removed on closing. `09` §9: in a campaign's export; format 2, a format-1 archive still importing. `10` §3: the hidden-information script places, edits, moves and deletes map notes. `11`: the refinements row. `13` §2 and §13: UXR-08 with exit criteria and derived characteristics. AGENTS.md's scope, play and hidden-information red lines name map notes. Defaults the owner's answers leave open, each open to the owner: the shortcut O; the icon 16 px across in the ember colour; snapped to a square's centre, Alt off the grid; an empty note removed when its popover closes; the whole list in each event.
payload.why: The amendment regime (D-002) requires the owner's answer in the specs, and `schema.test.ts` and `live.test.ts` read the entity and event tables of `03` §1 and `04` §3.
payload.alternatives: An implementation decision only (rejected: it crosses a red line and the entity count of `03` §1).

payload.title: UXR-08: map_note in migration 0014, four REST routes, mapNotes.updated with the whole list, archive format 2, and a Konva layer of icons with the token's click and hover
payload.decision: Within Q-128 and D-202. Storage: migration 0014 adds `map_note` (`id` uuid, `scene_id` cascading, `x`, `y` REAL refusing infinities, `notes` at most 20,000 characters), indexed by scene; additive, rollback the dated backup; `server/src/db/mapNotes.ts` lists by id, creates, updates, deletes and copies; `duplicateScene` copies them. Contract (`shared/src/mapNotes.ts`): MapNote, the create body (x, y within ±1e6, notes optional), the update body (strict, at least one field), `mapNotes.updated` {scene_id, map_notes}; `DmLiveSceneSchema.map_notes`; nothing in the players' schemas. Routes (`server/src/http/mapNotes.ts`): GET and POST `/api/scenes/:id/map-notes`, PATCH and DELETE `/api/map-notes/:id`, behind the /api guard; `mapNotesChanged` in ws/live.ts sends the dm room the live scene's whole list after each change, taking a dm version only. Archive: format 2, `data/mapnotes.json` (letters only, as the entry pattern asks), `counts.map_notes`; `migrateFormat` gives a format-1 archive an empty list and a count of none, and `readRecords` lets it lack the file; import checks each note's scene and gives it a new id through the scenes' map. DM view: `MapNoteLayer` draws each note as a 16 px icon (a page on a dark disc, ember ring, ringed in the text colour while open), inverse-scaled, with an 8 px larger hit area; click versus drag at DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX; a drop snapped to the square's centre, Alt to a thousandth of a square; the hover intent shared with tokens through `useHoverIntent`. `MapCanvas` takes the notes, their controls, a popover and a preview, listening only while tokens may be selected; placing a note is `Placing` with `kind: 'note'`, a one-square footprint whose centre is the note's point; Escape, a click on empty map and a pan close the popover; `data-map-notes` lists the icons for the end-to-end tests. `useMapNotes` reads a prepared scene's over REST and follows the live scene's from the dm room, showing each answer at once; `MapNotePopover` (class eg-note-popover, never eg-popover) holds NotesEditor under the draft key `mapnote:<id>` and Delete with an inline confirmation; `MapNotePreview` and `TokenPreview` share `PreviewCard`. A token's popover and a note's close each other; closing a note whose stored text is empty and with nothing typed waiting is deleting it.
payload.why: The whole list per event keeps the dm room's copy exact without per-change events and their ordering. Reusing Placing gives Enter, Escape, snapping, the crosshair and the clamp to the map for nothing. A class of its own keeps every test and locator of the token's popover meaning the token's.
payload.alternatives: One event per change (rejected: more types for a handful of small records); a separate placing mode in MapCanvas (rejected: duplicates Placing); drawing the icon in DOM over the canvas (rejected: it would not pan and zoom with the map without re-layout).

payload.title: UXR-07: D-199 restated: the initiative order reflows while dragged, numbers by the mouse wheel, and the TV's strip names the turn and the next, the round alone on a turn players cannot see
payload.decision: The owner's decision of 2026-10-06, recorded as card Q-127, answered A, as corrected by the owner on 2026-10-07. (1) While the DM drags a row of the initiative order, the other rows make room for it, sliding, so its slot shows where it will land; one reorder on the drop, none if it ends outside the list. (2) An initiative number may be stepped by the mouse wheel over its field, up raising it, an empty field starting at 10, sent once the wheel rests. (3) The TV's initiative strip shows two cards only, the entry whose turn it is and the next one, replaced on every turn; while the turn is an entry players cannot see, the strip shows the round alone, naming neither the turn nor the next, as the players' projection of `04` §4 has carried it since TBL-06.
payload.why: The owner asked for these on 2026-10-06. They override the strip of `08` §12 (a card for every visible entry, Q-111). Hidden information is unaffected: the players' projection of `04` §4 is unchanged and the strip shows a subset of it. Restated on 2026-10-07 after the UXR-07 review found that D-199 said a turn players cannot see showed the next card alone, which the projection never allows: naming the next entry on an unseen turn would let players place the unseen one. The owner kept the projection.
payload.alternatives: The DM-view changes only (rejected by the owner); the turn alone on the TV (rejected: the next player should see they are up); narrowing the players' projection to two entries (rejected: a change to the contract and the hidden-information suite for no gain, the projection already carrying only what players see).; on an unseen turn, the next card shown by widening the players' projection (rejected by the owner on 2026-10-07: it touches the hidden-information red line and hints where the unseen creature acts).

payload.title: UXR-07: D-201 restated after review: one notch is one step, Escape cancels the wheel, a held drag keeps up with the entries, the strip shows the round alone on an unseen turn
payload.decision: Within Q-127 and D-205; no contract or server change. (1) Wheel (`client/src/dm/initiative/wheel.ts`): a non-passive wheel listener on the number field, so the panel does not scroll under it; up adds one, down takes one, within -99 to 999; a line- or page-mode event is one step, and so is a single pixel-mode event of 50 px or more (a mouse notch, which Chromium reports as 100 px or more under display scaling); smaller pixel-mode deltas (trackpads) make one step per 50 px accumulated; an empty field starts at 10; each step shows at once and the number is sent once, 600 ms after the last step, or at once when the pointer leaves the field or it loses focus; Escape forgets the steps not yet sent along with the draft; Ctrl and the wheel is left to the browser's zoom. (2) Drag (`reorder.ts`, `InitiativePanel.tsx`): the order a held row builds is reconciled with the encounter's entries on every render, an entry gone dropped and a new one appended, so the drop sends every entry and is not refused as `order_mismatch`; rows slide by their place within the list, so content appearing above it slides none. (3) Strip (`client/src/player/InitiativeStrip.tsx`): the cards are the entries at the projection's `current` and `next`, in that order, `next` equal to `current` one card; on a turn players cannot see both are null and the strip shows the round alone (`04` §4, D-205); keyed by round, turn and entry, so each turn's cards fade in (300 ms, none under reduced motion).
payload.why: The UXR-07 review of 2026-10-07 found a mouse notch stepping by two or three, Escape leaving the wheel's steps to be sent, a drop refused when an entry arrived while a row was held, every row sliding when the offer appeared above the list, and D-201 describing a next card on an unseen turn that the projection never carries.
payload.alternatives: Counting a notch by its pixels (rejected: the step would depend on the browser and the display scaling); the wheel only while the field has focus (rejected in D-201); refusing a drag's drop when the entries changed and asking the DM to drag again (rejected: the reconciled order is what the DM meant, with the newcomer last as the server adds it).

payload.title: UXR-08 review: a note closed empty is removed by a guarded DELETE (if_empty, 409 map_note_not_empty); archive positions bounded as REST bounds them; a format-1 archive with map notes refused
payload.decision: Within Q-128 and D-202. (1) `DELETE /api/map-notes/:id?if_empty=true` (`MapNoteDeleteQuerySchema`, strict, the only accepted value the string `true`) removes the note only while its stored text is empty or blank (`hasNotes`, as the DM view judges a note empty), read and deleted in one transaction; a note holding text is kept and the request answers 409 with the new error code `map_note_not_empty`, telling no room; a DELETE without it, the one the DM confirms, stays unconditional. The DM view's removal of a note whose popover closes empty, and of one left open when the scene panel unmounts (a scene switch), uses it and on 409 keeps the note and reads the list again. (2) Opening a note's popover or placing a note deselects the token, so the token keys (arrows, H, Delete) cannot act on it unseen; Escape in the popover and a confirmed Delete return the focus to the map; a deleted note's unsaved draft is forgotten; a failed read of a scene's notes says so (`mapNotes.loadFailed`) with Retry. (3) Archives: a map note's and a token's x and y bounded at ±1,000,000, as their REST bodies are; a format-1 archive carrying `data/mapnotes.json` refused as not part of an archive (`import_unsafe_entry`). Archive format unchanged.
payload.why: The UXR-08 review of 2026-10-07: a second DM window on a prepared scene, whose list nothing refreshes, could delete a note another window had written into, judging it empty from its own stale copy; the token stayed selected under an open note; focus fell to the page; archives accepted positions REST refuses and silently dropped a stray file.
payload.alternatives: Re-reading the note before deleting it (rejected: still a race between the read and the delete; the server's transaction is the only place that can judge it); a strict empty string for `if_empty` (rejected: a blank note would be refused on every close and never removed); a version number on map notes for optimistic concurrency (rejected: a migration and a contract change larger than the case needs).

payload.title: sharp 0.35.4 -> 0.35.5 for GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w (librsvg, CVE-2026-96889); the package's libvips list moved to 8.18.7 and cairo's licence text to the MPL-1.1
payload.decision: Within D-080 and D-166. `server/package.json` takes `sharp` ^0.35.5 and the lockfile its prebuilt binaries, which carry sharp-libvips 1.3.4 (libvips 8.18.7, librsvg 2.63.2) on every platform, Windows' DLLs included. The vendored `scripts/package/licences/libvips-libraries.txt` names libvips 8.18.7 and copies the sharp-libvips 1.3.4 README's Licensing table, which now gives cairo as the Mozilla Public License 1.1, no longer 2.0; cairo being the only entry under a Mozilla licence, `MPL-2.0.txt` is replaced by the MPL 1.1 text from mozilla.org (`MPL-1.1.txt`) at the end of THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt. Image processing, its options and its API are unchanged.
payload.why: A high advisory against sharp below 0.35.5 for its bundled librsvg was published this week and failed audit · linux and audit · windows on the UXR-06..08 pull request; `make package` refuses a libvips other than the one its vendored list belongs to.
payload.alternatives: Lockfile only, leaving the range at ^0.35.4 (rejected: a fresh resolution could still pick the vulnerable version); keeping the MPL-2.0 text beside the 1.1 (rejected: nothing shipped is under it any more, and the notice should name the licences actually used).

payload.title: UXR-06 review: a preview hidden by any move of the camera, the keyboard's included, and given up with a token that is gone
payload.decision: Within Q-126 and D-195. The hover intent of a canvas layer (`useHoverIntent`, shared by the token and map-note layers) takes the ids of the items drawn and the camera as a key (`x,y,scale`, from MapCanvas). Any change of the camera cancels the wait and hides the preview, so a zoom or a pan from the keyboard (`+`, `-`, `0`, the arrow keys with nothing selected) hides it as the wheel already did. `HoverIntent.keep(ids)` cancels the wait and the preview of an item no longer drawn (deleted, or removed by another window), so a token put back by undo with the same id previews only after a new rest. No server, contract or player-view change.
payload.why: The UXR-06 review of 2026-10-07: zooming from the keyboard left the preview showing, the card following the token away from the pointer, against `08` §14; a previewed token deleted and restored by undo showed its preview again unasked, and the stale intent kept a later rest on it from asking again.
payload.alternatives: Clearing the preview in each keyboard camera branch of MapCanvas (rejected: every future camera change would need the same line, and the layer's intent would keep its stale state); hiding on scale changes only (rejected: a keyboard pan moves the token from under the pointer too).
